metadata.title: $K$-theory and topological cyclic homology of henselian pairs

extraction_notes.note: Remark 2.14 is an independent proof of Lemma 2.5 inside a remark environment; typed proof (alternative proves edge) rather than remark.
Remark 3.14 states a cited fact (Stacks 09XD) that subideals of henselian ideals are henselian; typed theorem/external rather than remark.
Examples 2.4, 3.3 and 3.10 introduce notation used throughout (THH of rings, short exact sequences, free henselian algebras); typed definition.

Introduction Theorems A, B, C, D, F and Definition 1.3 restate later results; kept the body versions with the intro copies in also_stated_at. Theorems E and G are weaker special cases and kept as own nodes with specializes edges.

The proof-sketch rule asks for rigor semi_formal on sketch proof nodes, but rigor is not allowed on proofs; omitted it on the proofs and put semi_formal on Proposition 2.27 whose only argument is 'analogous'.
Construction 4.17 (typed definition) contains Corollary 4.18 as a nested environment; the corollary is nested in the definition.

Historical list of known continuity cases (Section 5.1) and intro enumerations of special cases are not extracted; ubiquitous conventions (Sp, smash product, S^0, mapping spectra) got no definition nodes.

nodes.name: Invariant part of K-theory $K^{\mathrm{inv}}$
nodes.statement: For a ring $R$, we write $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)$ for the homotopy fiber of the cyclotomic trace $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$.
nodes.genus: homotopy fiber of the cyclotomic trace

nodes.name: Dundas--Goodwillie--McCarthy theorem
nodes.statement: Let $R \to R'$ be a map of rings which is a surjection with nilpotent kernel.\footnote{Or, more generally, a map of connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra such that $\pi_0R\rightarrow\pi_0R'$ is a surjection with nilpotent kernel} Then the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R')$ is an equivalence.
nodes.statement_short: $K^{\mathrm{inv}}$ is invariant under surjections with nilpotent kernel.
assumptions: $R \to R'$ be a map of rings which is a surjection with nilpotent kernel
conclusions: the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R')$ is an equivalence
nodes.label: DGMthm

nodes.name: Gabber rigidity theorem
nodes.statement: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair. Suppose $n$ is invertible in $R$. Then the map $K(R)/n \to K(R/I)/n$ is an equivalence of spectra.
nodes.statement_short: K-theory with coefficients invertible in $R$ is rigid for henselian pairs.
conclusions: the map $K(R)/n \to K(R/I)/n$ is an equivalence of spectra
nodes.label: gabberthm

nodes.name: Logarithmic differential forms $\Omega^i_{R,\mathrm{log}}$
nodes.statement: We let $\Omega^i_{R, \mathrm{log}}$ denote the subgroup of $\Omega^i_R$ consisting of elements which can be written as sums of products of forms $dx/x$ for $x$ a unit.

nodes.name: Geisser--Levine theorem
nodes.statement: The mod $p$ $K$-groups $K_i(R; \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}) = \pi_i( K(R)/p)$ are identified with the logarithmic forms $\Omega^{i}_{R, \mathrm{log}}$ for $i \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Mod $p$ K-groups of a regular local $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra are logarithmic forms.
conclusions: The mod $p$ $K$-groups $K_i(R; \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}) = \pi_i( K(R)/p)$ are identified with the logarithmic forms $\Omega^{i}_{R, \mathrm{log}}$ for $i \geq 0$

nodes.name: Pro Geisser--Levine theorem (mod $p$)
nodes.statement: For any regular local $F$-finite $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$ and ideal $I \subset R$, there is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups $\{K_i(R/I^n; \mathbb{Z}/p \mathbb{Z})\}_{n \geq 1} \simeq \left\{\Omega^i_{R/I^n, \mathrm{log}}\right\}_{n \geq 1}$ for each $i \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Pro mod $p$ K-groups of $R/I^n$ are pro logarithmic forms, for regular local F-finite $R$.
conclusions: there is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups $\{K_i(R/I^n; \mathbb{Z}/p \mathbb{Z})\}_{n \geq 1} \simeq \left\{\Omega^i_{R/I^n, \mathrm{log}}\right\}_{n \geq 1}$ for each $i \geq 0$

nodes.name: $\mathrm{TC}/p$ is finitary
nodes.statement: The construction $R \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$, from rings $R$ to spectra, commutes with filtered colimits.
conclusions: The construction $R \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$, from rings $R$ to spectra, commutes with filtered colimits

nodes.name: Category $\operatorname{CAlg}_{/R}$
nodes.statement: The category of commutative algebras over a ring $R$ is denoted by $\operatorname{CAlg}_{/R}$.

nodes.name: Subcategories $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq r}$, $\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq r}$
nodes.statement: Given an integer $r$, we let $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq r}$ (resp.~$\mathrm{Sp}_{\leq r}$) for the subcategory of $X \in\mathrm{Sp}$ such that $\pi_i(X) = 0$ for $i < r$ (resp.~$i>r$).

nodes.name: Truncation functors $\tau_{\geq r}, \tau_{\leq r}$
nodes.statement: We let $\tau_{\geq r}, \tau_{\leq r}$ denote the associated truncation functors.

nodes.name: Connective and nonconnective K-theory $K$, $\mathbb{K}$
nodes.statement: We let $K$ denote connective $K$-theory and $\mathbb{K}$ denote its nonconnective analog; $\mathrm{TC}$ denotes topological cyclic homology.

nodes.name: Relative K-theory $K(R,I)$, $\mathbb{K}(R,I)$
nodes.statement: Given a ring $R$ and an ideal $I \subset R$, we let $K(R, I)$ (resp.~$\mathbb{K}(R, I)$) denote the relative $K$-theory (resp.~relative nonconnective $K$-theory), defined as $\mathrm{fib}(K(R) \to K(R/I))$ and $\mathrm{fib}(\mathbb{K}(R) \to \mathbb{K}(R/I))$.

nodes.name: Relative $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R,I)$ and $\mathrm{TC}(R,I)$
nodes.statement: We define $ K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R, I), \mathrm{TC}(R, I)$ similarly.

nodes.name: Mod $p^r$ K-groups $K_*(R;\mathbb{Z}/p^r\mathbb{Z})$
nodes.statement: Finally, following traditional practice in algebraic $K$-theory, we will sometimes write $K_*(R; \mathbb{Z}/p^r \mathbb{Z})$ for the mod $p^r$ homotopy of the spectrum $K(R)$ (i.e., $\pi_*( K(R)/p^r)$) and similarly for $\mathrm{TC}$.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic spectrum
nodes.statement: A {\em cyclotomic spectrum} is a tuple $$ (X , \, \{\varphi_{X, p}: X \to X^{tC_p}\}_{p = 2, 3, 5, \dots }),$$ where $X \in \mathrm{Fun}(BS^1, \mathrm{Sp})$ is a spectrum with an $S^1$-action which is moreover equipped with a map $\varphi_p:X\to X^{tC_p}$ (the {\em cyclotomic Frobenius} at $p$), for each prime number $p$, which is required to be equivariant with respect to the $S^1$-action on $X$ and the $S^1\simeq S^1/C_p$-action on the Tate construction $X^{tC_p}$. By a standard abuse of notation we will occasionally denote a cyclotomic spectrum simply by the underlying spectrum $X$. For the precise definition of the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{CycSp}$ of cyclotomic spectra (whose objects are as above) as a lax equalizer, we refer the reader to \cite[II.1]{nikolaus-scholze}. See \cite[IV.2]{nikolaus-scholze} for a treatment of the symmetric monoidal structure.
nodes.statement_short: A spectrum with $S^1$-action and $S^1$-equivariant Frobenius maps $X \to X^{tC_p}$ for every prime $p$.
differentia: equipped with a map $\varphi_p:X\to X^{tC_p}$ (the {\em cyclotomic Frobenius} at $p$), for each prime number $p$

nodes.name: Topological cyclic homology of a cyclotomic spectrum
nodes.statement: Given $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}$, its \emph{topological cyclic homology} $\mathrm{TC}(X) $ is defined as the mapping spectrum $\mathrm{TC}(X) = \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{CycSp}}(\mathbf{1}, X)$, where $\mathbf{1} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ is the unit (cf.~Definition \ref{cons_trivial}). We moreover write \[ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) = X^{hS^1}, \quad \mathrm{TP}(X) = X^{tS^1}\] for its {\em negative topological cyclic homology} and \emph{periodic topological cyclic homology}, the latter having been particularly studied by Hesselholt \cite{hesselholt-tp}.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ is the mapping spectrum from the unit; also defines $\mathrm{TC}^-$ and $\mathrm{TP}$.
nodes.label: definition_TC_via_NS

nodes.name: Connective subcategories $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$ and $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$
nodes.statement: Given $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, let $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Sp}$ consisting of those spectra $X$ that satisfy $\pi_i(X) = 0$ for $i < n$. Let $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$ denote the full subcategory of $\mathrm{CycSp}$ consisting of those cyclotomic spectra $(X, \{\varphi_{X,p}\}_{p = 2, 3, 5, \dots} )$ such that the underlying spectrum $X$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$.

nodes.name: Nikolaus--Scholze formula for TC
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TC}(X) = \mathrm{fib}( \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\mathrm{can}_X - \varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X)),
nodes.label: keyformula

nodes.name: Topological Hochschild homology of a ring as a cyclotomic spectrum
nodes.statement: A key source of examples of cyclotomic spectra arises as follows. If $R$ is a ring (or, more generally, a structured ring spectrum), then one can form its topological Hochschild homology $\mathrm{THH}(R)$ as an object of $\mathrm{CycSp}$, following \cite[\S III.2]{nikolaus-scholze}. As usual, we will write $\mathrm{TC}(R), \mathrm{TC}^-(R), \mathrm{TP}(R)$ in place of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathrm{THH}(R)), \mathrm{TC}^-(\mathrm{THH}(R)), \mathrm{TP}(\mathrm{THH}(R))$.
nodes.statement_short: THH of a ring is a cyclotomic spectrum; $\mathrm{TC}(R)$, $\mathrm{TC}^-(R)$, $\mathrm{TP}(R)$ denote the invariants of $\mathrm{THH}(R)$.

nodes.name: Genuine fixed points $\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p)$ with $R$, $F$, $V$
nodes.statement: In particular, given $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ which is $p$-complete, one extracts genuine fixed point spectra $\mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p):=X^{C_{p^{r-1}}}$ for each $r\ge1$, which are related by Restriction ($R$), Frobenius ($F$), and Verschiebung ($V$) maps: \[ R, F: \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \to \mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p) , \quad V: \mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p) \to \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p).\]

nodes.name: Classical topological cyclic homology via TR
nodes.statement: Setting $\mathrm{TR}(X;p):=\varprojlim_R\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p)$, then the topological cyclic homology of $X$ is classically defined as \begin{equation} \mathrm{TC}(X)=\mathrm{fib}(\mathrm{TR}(X;p)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}-F}\mathrm{TR}(X;p)).\end{equation}

nodes.name: Classical formula for TC via TR
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TC}(X)=\mathrm{fib}(\mathrm{TR}(X;p)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}-F}\mathrm{TR}(X;p)).
nodes.label: keyformulaclassical

nodes.name: Connectivity of TC
nodes.statement: Suppose $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$ is $p$-complete. Then $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n-1}$.
conclusions: $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n-1}$
nodes.label: connectivity

nodes.name: Proof of Connectivity of TC
nodes.statement: Using formula (\ref{keyformulaclassical}), it suffices to show that $\mathrm{TR}(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$; using the Milnor sequence, it is therefore enough to prove that $\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$ and that the Restriction maps $R:\pi_n\mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \to \pi_n\mathrm{TR}^{r}(X;p)$ are surjective for all $r\ge1$. But this inductively follows from the basic cofiber sequence (cf.~\cite[Th.~1.2]{Hesselholt}) \begin{equation} X_{hC_{p^r}} \to \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \stackrel{R}{\to} \mathrm{TR}^r(X;p) \end{equation} and the observation that $X_{hC_{p^r}}\in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via the classical formula and Milnor sequence to connectivity of $\mathrm{TR}^r$, proved inductively from the isotropy separation sequence.

nodes.name: Isotropy separation cofiber sequence
nodes.statement: X_{hC_{p^r}} \to \mathrm{TR}^{r+1}(X;p) \stackrel{R}{\to} \mathrm{TR}^r(X;p)
nodes.label: isotropysep

nodes.name: TC/p commutes with geometric realizations
nodes.statement: The functor $ \mathrm{TC}/p:\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$, $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ commutes with geometric realizations.
conclusions: The functor $ \mathrm{TC}/p:\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$, $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ commutes with geometric realizations
nodes.label: geometricreal

nodes.name: Proof of TC/p commutes with geometric realizations
nodes.statement: A geometric realization of connective spectra agrees with its $n^{th}$ partial geometric realization in degrees $<n$. Since $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)/p=\mathrm{TC}(X/p)$ decreases connectivity at most by one by Lemma \ref{connectivity}, to show that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ commutes with geometric realizations it therefore suffices to show that it commutes with $n^{th}$ partial geometric realizations for all $n$. But these are finite colimits, and are thus preserved by $\mathrm{TC}/p$ since the latter is an exact functor.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric realizations agree with partial (finite) realizations in a range; TC/p is exact and lowers connectivity by at most one.

nodes.name: Reduce to partial realizations
nodes.statement: A geometric realization of connective spectra agrees with its $n^{th}$ partial geometric realization in degrees $<n$. Since $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)/p=\mathrm{TC}(X/p)$ decreases connectivity at most by one by Lemma \ref{connectivity}, to show that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ commutes with geometric realizations it therefore suffices to show that it commutes with $n^{th}$ partial geometric realizations for all $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Since TC/p lowers connectivity by at most one, reduce to $n$-th partial geometric realizations.

nodes.name: Finite colimits are preserved
nodes.statement: But these are finite colimits, and are thus preserved by $\mathrm{TC}/p$ since the latter is an exact functor.
nodes.statement_short: Partial realizations are finite colimits, preserved by the exact functor TC/p.

nodes.name: Cocontinuity of TC/p on connective cyclotomic spectra
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathrm{TC}/p: \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$, commutes with all colimits.
conclusions: The functor $\mathrm{TC}/p: \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Sp}$, commutes with all colimits
nodes.label: TCcommutes

nodes.name: TC commutes with limits of towers
nodes.statement: There is also a dual assertion which is significantly easier. Suppose we have a tower $\dots \to X_3 \to X_2 \to X_1$ in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. Then the inverse limit of the tower $\left\{X_i\right\}$ exists in $\mathrm{CycSp}$ (in fact, in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq -1}$) and is preserved by the forgetful functor $\mathrm{CycSp} \to \mathrm{Sp}$. Indeed, we have $(\varprojlim X_i)^{tC_p} \simeq \varprojlim X_i^{tC_p}$ because the $X_i$'s are uniformly bounded-below, and taking $C_p$-homotopy orbits behaves as a finite colimit in any range of degrees. Then we can appeal to the description of $\mathrm{CycSp}$ as a lax equalizer and \cite[Prop. II.1.5]{nikolaus-scholze}. In particular, it follows that if $X = \varprojlim X_i$ on the level of underlying spectra, then $\mathrm{TC}(X) \simeq \varprojlim \mathrm{TC}(X_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Inverse limits of towers of connective cyclotomic spectra exist, are computed underlying, and TC commutes with them.
nodes.label: TCinvlim

nodes.name: Trivial cyclotomic spectrum $X^{\mathrm{triv}}$
nodes.statement: We have a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathrm{CycSp}$, so it receives a unique symmetric monoidal, cocontinuous functor \[ \mathrm{Sp} \to \mathrm{CycSp},\quad X \mapsto X^{\mathrm{triv}} \] whose right adjoint is the functor $\mathrm{TC}: \mathrm{CycSp} \to \mathrm{Sp}$. More explicitly, this functor $X \mapsto X^{\mathrm{triv}}$ can be identified as follows: $X^\sub{triv}$ has underlying spectrum $X$ equipped with the trivial $S^1$-action; there is therefore a resulting $S^1$-equivariant map $X \to X^{hC_p} = F(BC_{p+}, X)$, and the cyclotomic Frobenius at $p$ for $X^\sub{triv}$ is the composition $\varphi_{X,p}:X\to X^{hC_p} \to X^{tC_p}$. (Notation: when $X$ is a $p$-complete spectrum for a particular prime number $p$, we will tend to drop the $p$ from $\varphi_{X,p}$.) Compare the discussion on \cite[p. 126]{nikolaus-scholze}. For example, taking $X$ to be the sphere spectrum $S^0 \in \mathrm{Sp}$ obtains the {\em cyclotomic sphere spectrum}, which is moreover the unit $\mathbf{1} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$.
nodes.statement_short: The symmetric monoidal left adjoint of TC sends $X$ to $X$ with trivial circle action and Frobenius through $X^{hC_p}$.
nodes.label: cons_trivial

nodes.name: Frobenius annihilates $x$
nodes.statement: The Frobenius map $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}:\mathrm{TC}^-_*( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}_*(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$ annihilates $x$.
nodes.statement_short: The Frobenius $\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})\to\mathrm{TP}$ kills the degree $-2$ generator $x$.
conclusions: The Frobenius map $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}:\mathrm{TC}^-_*( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}_*(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$ annihilates $x$
nodes.label: Frobvanish

nodes.name: Proof of Frobenius annihilates $x$
nodes.statement: There is a commutative diagram of spectra \[ \xymatrix{ \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]^-{\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}} \ar[d]& \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[d] \\ H\mathbb{F}_p \ar[r]_{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}} & H \mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p} }\] where the top row is obtained by taking $S^1$-homotopy fixed points on the bottom row via the Tate orbit lemma, \cite[Lem.~II.4.2]{nikolaus-scholze}. The right vertical map $\mathrm{TP}(H\mathbb F_p^\sub{triv})\to H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p}$ is an isomorphism in degree $-2$: indeed, the degree $-2$ generator is invertible in the source by the above calculation of $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb F_p^\sub{triv})$, and therefore necessarily maps to a generator of $\pi_{-2}(H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p})$ by multiplicativity. Going both ways around the diagram and noting that of course $\pi_{-2}(H\mathbb F_p)=0$, we find that $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}$ must be zero on $\pi_{-2}( \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare the Frobenius on $\mathrm{TC}^-$ with that on $H\mathbb{F}_p$ via the Tate orbit lemma; degree reasons force $x\mapsto 0$.

nodes.name: Compare Frobenius maps
nodes.statement: There is a commutative diagram of spectra \[ \xymatrix{ \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]^-{\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}} \ar[d]& \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[d] \\ H\mathbb{F}_p \ar[r]_{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}} & H \mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p} }\] where the top row is obtained by taking $S^1$-homotopy fixed points on the bottom row via the Tate orbit lemma, \cite[Lem.~II.4.2]{nikolaus-scholze}.
nodes.statement_short: Relate the Frobenius on $\mathrm{TC}^-$ to that on $H\mathbb{F}_p$ via the Tate orbit lemma.

nodes.name: Right vertical map is iso in degree $-2$
nodes.statement: The right vertical map $\mathrm{TP}(H\mathbb F_p^\sub{triv})\to H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p}$ is an isomorphism in degree $-2$: indeed, the degree $-2$ generator is invertible in the source by the above calculation of $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb F_p^\sub{triv})$, and therefore necessarily maps to a generator of $\pi_{-2}(H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p})$ by multiplicativity.
nodes.statement_short: The map $\mathrm{TP}\to H\mathbb{F}_p^{tC_p}$ is an isomorphism in degree $-2$ by multiplicativity.

nodes.name: Degree argument
nodes.statement: Going both ways around the diagram and noting that of course $\pi_{-2}(H\mathbb F_p)=0$, we find that $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}$ must be zero on $\pi_{-2}( \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}))$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $\pi_{-2}H\mathbb{F}_p=0$, the Frobenius vanishes on $\pi_{-2}$.

nodes.name: Alternative argument for the Frobenius lemma via $\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{F}_p)$
nodes.statement: In fact, noting that $\mathrm{TC}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ receives a map $H\mathbb{Z}_p \to \mathrm{TC}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ (the source is the connective cover of the target) we obtain a map of cyclotomic spectra $H \mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{triv}} \to \mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{F}_p)$, which can be used to recover Lemma \ref{Frobvanish} from the more precise assertions about the cyclotomic spectrum $\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{F}_p)$.
nodes.statement_short: Map $H\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}\to\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ and use the known structure of $\mathrm{THH}(\mathbb{F}_p)$.

nodes.name: Cofiber sequences for circle actions on $H\mathbb{Z}$-modules
nodes.statement: Let $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{Z}}(\mathrm{Sp}^{BS^1})$ be an $H \mathbb{Z}$-module spectrum equipped with an $S^1$-action. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item There is a functorial cofiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}$-module spectra \[ \Sigma^{-2} X^{hS^1} \stackrel{x}{\longrightarrow} X^{hS^1} \longrightarrow X, \] where the first map is given by multiplication by the generator $x \in \pi_{-2}(H \mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}) = H^2( \mathbb{CP}^\infty; \mathbb{Z})$. \item There is a functorial cofiber sequence of $H \mathbb{Z}$-modules \[ X \to X_{hS^1} \to \Sigma^2 X_{hS^1} . \] \item There is moreover a functorial cofiber sequence \[ \Sigma^{-2} X^{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x \mathrm{can}_X} X^{tS^1} \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}, \] where $\mathrm{can}_X: X^{hS^1} \to X^{tS^1}$ is the canonical map. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Three functorial cofiber sequences relating $X^{hS^1}$, $X^{tS^1}$, $X_{hS^1}$ and $X$ for an $H\mathbb{Z}$-module with circle action.
assumptions: $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{Z}}(\mathrm{Sp}^{BS^1})$ be an $H \mathbb{Z}$-module spectrum equipped with an $S^1$-action
conclusions: There is a functorial cofiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}$-module spectra \[ \Sigma^{-2} X^{hS^1} \stackrel{x}{\longrightarrow} X^{hS^1} \longrightarrow X, \]
There is a functorial cofiber sequence of $H \mathbb{Z}$-modules \[ X \to X_{hS^1} \to \Sigma^2 X_{hS^1} . \]
There is moreover a functorial cofiber sequence \[ \Sigma^{-2} X^{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x \mathrm{can}_X} X^{tS^1} \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}, \]
nodes.label: cofiberofx

nodes.name: Proof of Cofiber sequences for circle actions on $H\mathbb{Z}$-modules
nodes.statement: Assertion (1) is \cite[Lemma~IV.4.12]{nikolaus-scholze}, in view of the cofiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$-modules $\Sigma^{-2} H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x} H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}$. For assertion (2), by \emph{loc.~cit.}, we have functorial equivalences $X^{tS^1} \simeq X^{hS^1} \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}} H\mathbb{Z}^{tS^1} = X^{hS^1}[1/x]$. The fiber sequences $\Sigma (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}^{tS^1}$ and $\Sigma X_{hS^1} \to X^{hS^1} \to X^{tS^1}$ make $(H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$ into an $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} $-module and yield a natural equivalence $X_{hS^1} \simeq X^{hS^1} \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}} (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$. Using the fiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$-modules $H\mathbb{Z} \to (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x} \Sigma^2 (H \mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$, we obtain the assertion (2). Assertion (3) follows from assertion (1) and from the cofiber sequence $X^{hS^1} \stackrel{\mathrm{can}_X}{\to} X^{tS^1} \to \Sigma^2 X_{hS^1}$, where we use that multiplication by $x$ is an equivalence on $X^{tS^1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Nikolaus--Scholze for (1); derive (2) and (3) from module structures over $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$ and the norm cofiber sequence.

nodes.name: Assertion (1)
nodes.statement: Assertion (1) is \cite[Lemma~IV.4.12]{nikolaus-scholze}, in view of the cofiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$-modules $\Sigma^{-2} H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x} H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Nikolaus--Scholze.

nodes.name: Assertion (2)
nodes.statement: For assertion (2), by \emph{loc.~cit.}, we have functorial equivalences $X^{tS^1} \simeq X^{hS^1} \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}} H\mathbb{Z}^{tS^1} = X^{hS^1}[1/x]$. The fiber sequences $\Sigma (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} \to H\mathbb{Z}^{tS^1}$ and $\Sigma X_{hS^1} \to X^{hS^1} \to X^{tS^1}$ make $(H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$ into an $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1} $-module and yield a natural equivalence $X_{hS^1} \simeq X^{hS^1} \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}} (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$. Using the fiber sequence of $H\mathbb{Z}^{hS^1}$-modules $H\mathbb{Z} \to (H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1} \xrightarrow{x} \Sigma^2 (H \mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$, we obtain the assertion (2).
nodes.statement_short: Express $X_{hS^1}$ as a base change of $(H\mathbb{Z})_{hS^1}$ and use its cofiber sequence.

nodes.name: Assertion (3)
nodes.statement: Assertion (3) follows from assertion (1) and from the cofiber sequence $X^{hS^1} \stackrel{\mathrm{can}_X}{\to} X^{tS^1} \to \Sigma^2 X_{hS^1}$, where we use that multiplication by $x$ is an equivalence on $X^{tS^1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine (1) with the norm cofiber sequence, $x$ being invertible on $X^{tS^1}$.

nodes.name: Fiber sequence for TC of $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules
nodes.statement: For $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}( \mathrm{CycSp})$, there exists a functorial fiber sequence \begin{equation} \mathrm{TC}(X) \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For modules over trivial $H\mathbb{F}_p$, TC is the fiber of $X\to X_{hS^1}$.
conclusions: there exists a functorial fiber sequence \begin{equation} \mathrm{TC}(X) \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}. \end{equation}
nodes.label: functorialfibseq

nodes.name: TC as fiber of $X \to X_{hS^1}$
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TC}(X) \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X_{hS^1}.

nodes.name: Proof of Fiber sequence for TC of $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules
nodes.statement: We show first that, for $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) $, the composition \begin{equation} \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xTo{x} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X) \end{equation} is functorially nullhomotopic. In fact, since $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, we find that $\mathrm{TC}^-(X)$ is an $\mathrm{TC}^-( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, $\mathrm{TP}(X)$ is a $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, and the map $\varphi_X$ is $\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}$-linear. We obtain a resulting functorial commutative diagram, where the base-changes are along $\varphi_{ H \mathbb F_p}: \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$, \begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=1cm{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d] \ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & \mathrm{TP}(X) } .\end{equation} However $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}(x)$ vanishes, by Lemma~\ref{Frobvanish}, and so the composite \eqref{th} is functorially nullhomotopic as desired. It now follows that there is a functorial commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d]_{x} \ar[r]^{\mathrm{id}} &\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X)\ar[d]^{x \mathrm{can}_X} \\ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]_{\mathrm{can}_X-\varphi_X} & \mathrm{TP}(X) } \end{equation} in which the fiber of the bottom arrow is $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ by formula \eqref{keyformula}. Therefore $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ is also the fiber of the natural map $X \to X_{hS^1}$ between the cofibers of the vertical arrows in the above diagram, where we identify the cofibers using Lemma~\ref{cofiberofx}.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\varphi\circ x$ is nullhomotopic by linearity over $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$ and Frobenius killing $x$; then compare cofibers of $x$ and $x\,\mathrm{can}$.

nodes.name: Composite $\varphi_X\circ x$ is nullhomotopic
nodes.statement: We show first that, for $X \in \mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) $, the composition \begin{equation} \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xTo{x} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X) \end{equation} is functorially nullhomotopic. In fact, since $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, we find that $\mathrm{TC}^-(X)$ is an $\mathrm{TC}^-( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, $\mathrm{TP}(X)$ is a $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, and the map $\varphi_X$ is $\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}$-linear. We obtain a resulting functorial commutative diagram, where the base-changes are along $\varphi_{ H \mathbb F_p}: \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$, \begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=1cm{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d] \ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & \mathrm{TP}(X) } .\end{equation} However $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}(x)$ vanishes, by Lemma~\ref{Frobvanish}, and so the composite \eqref{th} is functorially nullhomotopic as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\varphi_X\circ x$ is functorially nullhomotopic.

nodes.name: Composite of $x$ and Frobenius
nodes.statement: \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xTo{x} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \xrightarrow{\varphi_X} \mathrm{TP}(X)
nodes.label: th

nodes.name: Module structures
nodes.statement: In fact, since $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, we find that $\mathrm{TC}^-(X)$ is an $\mathrm{TC}^-( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, $\mathrm{TP}(X)$ is a $\mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$-module, and the map $\varphi_X$ is $\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}$-linear.
nodes.statement_short: $\varphi_X$ is linear over the Frobenius of $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$.

nodes.name: Base-change diagram
nodes.statement: We obtain a resulting functorial commutative diagram, where the base-changes are along $\varphi_{ H \mathbb F_p}: \mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \to \mathrm{TP}( H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})$, \begin{equation} \xymatrix@C=1cm{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d] \ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & \mathrm{TP}(X) } .\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Factor through base change along the Frobenius.

nodes.name: Base-change diagram along the Frobenius of $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$
nodes.statement: \xymatrix@C=1cm{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]^x \ar[d] & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d] \ar[rd]^{\varphi_X} \\ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r]_-{\varphi_{H \mathbb F_p}(x)} & \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \otimes_{\mathrm{TC}^-(H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})} \mathrm{TP}(H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}) \ar[r] & \mathrm{TP}(X) } .
nodes.label: cycdiag

nodes.name: Frobenius kills $x$
nodes.statement: However $\varphi_{H \mathbb{F}_p}(x)$ vanishes, by Lemma~\ref{Frobvanish}, and so the composite \eqref{th} is functorially nullhomotopic as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Frobenius lemma.

nodes.name: Compare $\mathrm{can}-\varphi$ with $x\,\mathrm{can}$
nodes.statement: It now follows that there is a functorial commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d]_{x} \ar[r]^{\mathrm{id}} &\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X)\ar[d]^{x \mathrm{can}_X} \\ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]_{\mathrm{can}_X-\varphi_X} & \mathrm{TP}(X) } \end{equation} in which the fiber of the bottom arrow is $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ by formula \eqref{keyformula}.
nodes.statement_short: Obtain a square whose bottom fiber is TC by the NS formula.

nodes.name: Diagram comparing $\mathrm{can}-\varphi$ with $x\,\mathrm{can}$
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ \Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[d]_{x} \ar[r]^{\mathrm{id}} &\Sigma^{-2} \mathrm{TC}^-(X)\ar[d]^{x \mathrm{can}_X} \\ \mathrm{TC}^-(X) \ar[r]_{\mathrm{can}_X-\varphi_X} & \mathrm{TP}(X) }
nodes.label: cyc2

nodes.name: Identify fiber via cofibers
nodes.statement: Therefore $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ is also the fiber of the natural map $X \to X_{hS^1}$ between the cofibers of the vertical arrows in the above diagram, where we identify the cofibers using Lemma~\ref{cofiberofx}.
nodes.statement_short: TC is the fiber of $X\to X_{hS^1}$ using the cofiber sequences lemma.

nodes.name: TC commutes with colimits on $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) \to \mathrm{Sp}$ given by $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)$ commutes with all colimits. That is, the unit of the presentably symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp})$ is compact.
conclusions: The functor $\mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp}) \to \mathrm{Sp}$ given by $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X)$ commutes with all colimits
the unit of the presentably symmetric monoidal stable $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Mod}_{H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}}(\mathrm{CycSp})$ is compact
nodes.label: Fpcommutecolimit

nodes.name: Proof of TC commutes with colimits on $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules
nodes.statement: Since passage to homotopy orbits commutes with all colimits, this follows from Proposition \ref{functorialfibseq}.
nodes.statement_short: Homotopy orbits commute with colimits; apply the fiber sequence.

nodes.name: Proof of the connectivity lemma via Nikolaus--Scholze
nodes.statement: Let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{ \geq 0}$ be $p$-complete. Using the functorial fiber sequence of Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}, we can give an independent proof of Lemma~\ref{connectivity} (and thus of Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}) which is independent of the classical approach to $\mathrm{TC}$ (i.e., based entirely on the formula \eqref{keyformula}). Namely, we argue that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$. First, suppose that $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module. In this case, we find that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ thanks to Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}. More generally, if $X$ is a $p$-complete $H \mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, then we find that $X/p$ is an $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module so that $\mathrm{TC}(X/p) \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$; by $p$-completeness we deduce that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$. In general, let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ be an arbitrary $p$-complete object. Then, we consider the Adams tower for $X$ with respect to the commutative algebra object $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$, i.e., the tower for the totalization of the cosimplicial object $X \otimes (H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}})^{\otimes \bullet + 1}$ (cf.~\cite[Sec.~2.1]{MNN17} for a reference in this generality). That is, we consider the tower $\left\{X_n\right\} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ defined inductively such that $X_0 = X$ and $X_{n+1}$ is the fiber of the map $X_{n} \to X_n \otimes H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$. One sees easily that $X_n \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$, and that $X_n$ is $p$-complete since $\pi_i(S^0)$ is finite for $i>0$. Since $X_{n}/X_{n+1}$ is a $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, it follows from the previous analysis that $\mathrm{TC}(X_n/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq (n-1)}$ for each $n$. Inductively, it follows now that $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) = \mathrm{TC}(X_0/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for each $n$ and that the maps $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) \to \mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n})$ are surjective on $\pi_{-1}$. Since $X \to X/X_{n+1}$ is an equivalence in degrees $\leq n$, it follows (as in \cite[Lem.~I.2.6]{nikolaus-scholze}) that \[ X^{hS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n )^{hS^1}, \quad X^{tS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n)^{tS^1} \] and therefore by \eqref{keyformula} \[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \simeq \varprojlim \mathrm{TC}(X/X_n). \] Using the Milnor exact sequence and the connectivity properties of $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1})$, one concludes that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Prove $\mathrm{TC}(X)\in\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ first for $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules via the fiber sequence, then in general by an Adams tower for $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$ and the Milnor sequence.
nodes.label: rem:TCconnectivity

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: Let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{ \geq 0}$ be $p$-complete. Using the functorial fiber sequence of Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}, we can give an independent proof of Lemma~\ref{connectivity} (and thus of Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}) which is independent of the classical approach to $\mathrm{TC}$ (i.e., based entirely on the formula \eqref{keyformula}). Namely, we argue that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\mathrm{TC}(X)\in\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.

nodes.name: Module case
nodes.statement: First, suppose that $X$ is an $H \mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module. In this case, we find that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ thanks to Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq}. More generally, if $X$ is a $p$-complete $H \mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, then we find that $X/p$ is an $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module so that $\mathrm{TC}(X/p) \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$ belongs to $\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$; by $p$-completeness we deduce that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fiber sequence for $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules; extend to $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules.

nodes.name: Adams tower
nodes.statement: In general, let $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ be an arbitrary $p$-complete object. Then, we consider the Adams tower for $X$ with respect to the commutative algebra object $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$, i.e., the tower for the totalization of the cosimplicial object $X \otimes (H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}})^{\otimes \bullet + 1}$ (cf.~\cite[Sec.~2.1]{MNN17} for a reference in this generality). That is, we consider the tower $\left\{X_n\right\} \in \mathrm{CycSp}$ defined inductively such that $X_0 = X$ and $X_{n+1}$ is the fiber of the map $X_{n} \to X_n \otimes H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$. One sees easily that $X_n \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq n}$, and that $X_n$ is $p$-complete since $\pi_i(S^0)$ is finite for $i>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Adams tower for $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$.

nodes.name: Induction and limit
nodes.statement: Since $X_{n}/X_{n+1}$ is a $H\mathbb{Z}^{\mathrm{triv}}$-module, it follows from the previous analysis that $\mathrm{TC}(X_n/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq (n-1)}$ for each $n$. Inductively, it follows now that $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) = \mathrm{TC}(X_0/X_{n+1}) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for each $n$ and that the maps $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1}) \to \mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n})$ are surjective on $\pi_{-1}$. Since $X \to X/X_{n+1}$ is an equivalence in degrees $\leq n$, it follows (as in \cite[Lem.~I.2.6]{nikolaus-scholze}) that \[ X^{hS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n )^{hS^1}, \quad X^{tS^1} \simeq \varprojlim (X/X_n)^{tS^1} \] and therefore by \eqref{keyformula} \[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \simeq \varprojlim \mathrm{TC}(X/X_n). \] Using the Milnor exact sequence and the connectivity properties of $\mathrm{TC}(X/X_{n+1})$, one concludes that $\mathrm{TC}(X) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Connectivity of layers and Milnor sequence.

nodes.name: Proof of Cocontinuity of TC/p on connective cyclotomic spectra
nodes.statement: Consider an $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete. Since $\mathrm{TC}(X\otimes (-)^{\mathrm{triv}})$ is an exact functor from spectra to spectra with value $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ on $S^0$, we get a natural transformation \[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes (-) \to \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes (-)^{\mathrm{triv}}),\] uniquely characterized by being an equivalence on $S^0$, hence on any finite spectrum.\footnote{This is a standard ``assembly map". To construct it rigorously, note that left Kan extension of the restriction of the right hand side to finite spectra is uniquely characterized by its value on $S^0$, by the universal property of spectra among presentable stable $\infty$-categories, and therefore identifies with the left hand side.} By Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}, it is also an equivalence on any geometric realization of finite connective spectra, i.e., for any connective spectrum whose homology groups are finitely generated, e.g., $H \mathbb F_p$. So we have shown that, for any $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete, there is a natural equivalence $$\mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}).$$ Replacing $X$ with $X/p$, the same conclusion follows for an arbitrary $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. Then from Corollary~\ref{Fpcommutecolimit} we deduce that the functor $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p$ commutes with colimits in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$. Hence, given a diagram $I\to\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$, the induced map of spectra \begin{equation} \varinjlim_I \mathrm{TC}(X_i) \to \mathrm{TC}(X) \end{equation} becomes an equivalence after smashing with $H\mathbb{F}_p$. Since both sides are bounded below mod $p$ by Lemma \ref{connectivity}, it follows that \eqref{TCcolim} is an equivalence after smashing with $S^0/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Assembly map $\mathrm{TC}(X)\otimes(-)\to\mathrm{TC}(X\otimes(-)^{\mathrm{triv}})$ is an equivalence on $H\mathbb{F}_p$; reduce to $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules where TC is cocontinuous. Bounded-belowness then upgrades to mod $p$.

nodes.name: Assembly map
nodes.statement: Consider an $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete. Since $\mathrm{TC}(X\otimes (-)^{\mathrm{triv}})$ is an exact functor from spectra to spectra with value $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ on $S^0$, we get a natural transformation \[ \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes (-) \to \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes (-)^{\mathrm{triv}}),\] uniquely characterized by being an equivalence on $S^0$, hence on any finite spectrum.\footnote{This is a standard ``assembly map". To construct it rigorously, note that left Kan extension of the restriction of the right hand side to finite spectra is uniquely characterized by its value on $S^0$, by the universal property of spectra among presentable stable $\infty$-categories, and therefore identifies with the left hand side.}
nodes.statement_short: Construct the assembly map, an equivalence on finite spectra.

nodes.name: Extend to $H\mathbb{F}_p$
nodes.statement: By Corollary~\ref{geometricreal}, it is also an equivalence on any geometric realization of finite connective spectra, i.e., for any connective spectrum whose homology groups are finitely generated, e.g., $H \mathbb F_p$. So we have shown that, for any $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ which is $p$-complete, there is a natural equivalence $$\mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p \simeq \mathrm{TC}(X \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}).$$
nodes.statement_short: By commutation with geometric realizations, the assembly map is an equivalence on $H\mathbb{F}_p$.

nodes.name: Remove $p$-completeness
nodes.statement: Replacing $X$ with $X/p$, the same conclusion follows for an arbitrary $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to $X/p$.

nodes.name: Cocontinuity after smashing with $H\mathbb{F}_p$
nodes.statement: Then from Corollary~\ref{Fpcommutecolimit} we deduce that the functor $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X) \otimes H\mathbb{F}_p$ commutes with colimits in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use cocontinuity of TC on $H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}}$-modules.

nodes.name: Comparison map
nodes.statement: Hence, given a diagram $I\to\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$, the induced map of spectra \begin{equation} \varinjlim_I \mathrm{TC}(X_i) \to \mathrm{TC}(X) \end{equation} becomes an equivalence after smashing with $H\mathbb{F}_p$.
nodes.statement_short: The colimit comparison map becomes an equivalence after smashing with $H\mathbb{F}_p$.

nodes.name: Assembly map for TC of a colimit
nodes.statement: \varinjlim_I \mathrm{TC}(X_i) \to \mathrm{TC}(X)
nodes.label: TCcolim

nodes.name: Bounded below upgrade
nodes.statement: Since both sides are bounded below mod $p$ by Lemma \ref{connectivity}, it follows that \eqref{TCcolim} is an equivalence after smashing with $S^0/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded below spectra: $H\mathbb{F}_p$-equivalence implies mod $p$ equivalence.

nodes.name: Connective associative ring spectra $\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})$ be the $\infty$-category of connective associative ring spectra.

nodes.name: TC/p of connective ring spectra commutes with sifted colimits
nodes.statement: The functor $\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $R \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$ commutes with sifted colimits.
conclusions: The functor $\mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0})\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $R \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$ commutes with sifted colimits
nodes.label: TCring

nodes.name: Proof of TC/p of connective ring spectra commutes with sifted colimits
nodes.statement: This follows from Theorem~\ref{TCcommutes} since $\mathrm{TC}(R) = \mathrm{TC}( \mathrm{THH}(R))$, where we note that the topological Hochschild homology functor $\mathrm{THH}: \mathrm{Alg}(\mathrm{Sp}_{\geq 0}) \to \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$ commutes with sifted colimits (as geometric realizations and tensor products do).
nodes.statement_short: Write $\mathrm{TC}(R)=\mathrm{TC}(\mathrm{THH}(R))$ and use that THH commutes with sifted colimits.

nodes.name: Finitarity of TC/p for $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras via de Rham--Witt
nodes.statement: For commutative $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, Corollary~\ref{TCring} can be deduced using the description of Hesselholt \cite{Hesselholt} of $\mathrm{THH}$ of smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras in terms of the de Rham--Witt complex; we detail this in subsection~\ref{dRWapproach} below.

nodes.name: $p$-limit axiom for square-zero extensions
nodes.statement: In the case of square-zero extensions, the verification (called the \emph{$p$-limit axiom}) of Corollary~\ref{TCring} plays an important role in the proof that relative $K$-theory and $\mathrm{TC}$ with finite coefficients agree for nilimmersions of rings in McCarthy \cite{mccarthy}.

nodes.name: TC/p of spherical monoid rings
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be an $\mathbb{E}_1$-monoid in the $\infty$-category of spaces, so that one can form the spherical monoid ring $\Sigma^\infty_+ M$. The formula for $\mathrm{TC}$ of spherical monoid rings \cite[Lemma IV.3.1]{nikolaus-scholze} (preceded by the formula for spherical group rings appearing already in \cite[Eq. (0.3)]{BHM}) shows that for any such $R$, the cyclotomic structure map $\mathrm{THH}(R) \to \mathrm{THH}(R)^{tC_p}$ factors $S^1$-equivariantly through $\mathrm{THH}(R)^{hC_p}$, which is called a \emph{Frobenius lift} in \cite{nikolaus-scholze}. For cyclotomic spectrum $X$ with a Frobenius lift, the construction of ($p$-complete) $\mathrm{TC}$ simplifies: one has a fiber square \cite[Prop. IV-3.4]{nikolaus-scholze} relating $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ to $\Sigma X_{hS^1}$ and two copies of $X$. It follows from this that the construction $M \mapsto \mathrm{TC}( \Sigma^\infty_+ M)/p$ commutes with filtered colimits in $M$. Since the free associative algebra is a spherical monoid ring, and since $\mathrm{TC}$ is already known to commute with geometric realizations, one can also deduce Corollary~\ref{TCring} in this way.
nodes.statement_short: Via Frobenius lifts, $M\mapsto\mathrm{TC}(\Sigma^\infty_+M)/p$ commutes with filtered colimits, recovering the sifted-colimit corollary.

nodes.name: Approximation of TC/p by homotopy orbits
nodes.statement: For any given integer $n$, there exists a functor $F \in \mathrm{Fun}_{}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item $F$ belongs to the thick subcategory of $\mathrm{Fun}_{}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ generated by the functor $X \mapsto (X\otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^\sub{triv})_{hS^1}$; \item There exists an equivalence $\tau_{\leq n} F(X) \simeq \tau_{\leq n}(\mathrm{TC}(X)/p)$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: In any range, $\mathrm{TC}/p$ agrees with a functor in the thick subcategory generated by $X\mapsto(X\otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^{\mathrm{triv}})_{hS^1}$.
conclusions: there exists a functor $F \in \mathrm{Fun}_{}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}, \mathrm{Sp})$ with the following properties
nodes.label: strong:finiteness

nodes.name: Proof of Approximation of TC/p by homotopy orbits
nodes.statement: We claim that for each $n$, the functor $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}(X\otimes \tau_{\leq n+1}(S^0/p)^\sub{triv})$ has the desired properties. Indeed, it belongs to the thick subcategory generated by $X \mapsto (X\otimes H\mathbb{F}_p^\sub{triv})_{hS^1}$ thanks to Proposition~\ref{functorialfibseq} and assertion~(\ref{hS1cofib}) of Lemma~\ref{cofiberofx}, while the connectivity assertion follows from Lemma~\ref{connectivity}.
nodes.statement_short: Take $X\mapsto\mathrm{TC}(X\otimes\tau_{\leq n+1}(S^0/p)^{\mathrm{triv}})$ and use the fiber sequence and connectivity.

nodes.name: Finite-stage topological cyclic homology $\mathrm{TC}^r(X;p)$
nodes.statement: Given $X \in \mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}$, the classical approach to topological cyclic homology (cf.~subsection \ref{subsection_reminders}) involves the spectra \[ \mathrm{TC}^r(X;p) = \mathrm{fib}(\mathrm{TR}^r(X;p) \xrightarrow{R-F} \mathrm{TR}^{r-1}(X;p)) \] for all $r\ge1$.

nodes.name: Connectivity and cocontinuity of $\mathrm{TC}^r$
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathrm{TC}^r(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for all $r\ge1$ (by the proof of Lemma \ref{connectivity}), and that each functor $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}^r(X;p)$ commutes with all colimits (by induction using (\ref{isotropysep})).
conclusions: $\mathrm{TC}^r(X;p) \in \mathrm{Sp}_{\geq -1}$ for all $r\ge1$
each functor $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0}\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $X \mapsto \mathrm{TC}^r(X;p)$ commutes with all colimits

nodes.name: Pro-vanishing criterion for towers of functors to abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category admitting countable coproducts, and consider a tower of functors $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \operatorname{Ab}$, say $\ldots \rightarrow F_r\rightarrow F_{r-1}\rightarrow \ldots \rightarrow F_1$. Suppose that: \begin{enumerate} \item For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r F_r(X) = 0$. \item For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts. \end{enumerate} Then the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero, i.e.\ it is zero as an object of $\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Ab}))$; or, equivalently, for all $r\in\mathbb{N}$ there is an $s>r$ such that the morphism $F_s\rightarrow F_r$ is $0$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{C}$ be a category admitting countable coproducts
For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r F_r(X) = 0$.
For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts.
conclusions: the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero
nodes.label: invlimmzero

nodes.name: Proof of Pro-vanishing criterion for towers of functors to abelian groups
nodes.statement: First we show the weaker claim that for all $X\in\mathcal{C}$, the tower $\{F_r(X)\}_r$ of abelian groups is pro-zero. Set $M_r = F_r(X)$ for brevity. From the hypothesis we find that an infinite direct sum of copies of the tower $\{M_r\}_r$ has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$; thus \cite[Cor.~6]{Emmanouil} implies that $\{M_r\}_r$ is Mittag--Leffler, i.e., for each $r$, the descending sequence $\{\mathrm{im}(M_s \to M_r)\}_{s \geq r}$ of submodules of $M_r$ stabilizes. If this stable submodule were nonzero for some $r$, we would deduce the existence of a nonzero element of $\varprojlim_s M_s$, contradicting the hypothesis. Thus the stable value is $0$ for all $r$, which exactly means that $\{M_r\}_r$ is pro-zero. Now, suppose the claim of the lemma does not hold, i.e., that $\{F_r\}_r$ is not pro-zero. Then for each $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $s>r$, we can find an $Y\in\mathcal{C}$ such that $F_s(Y)\rightarrow F_r(Y)$ is nonzero. Let $X$ denote the coproduct over all pairs $s>r$ of a choice of such a $Y$. Then for every $s>r$ the map $F_s(X)\rightarrow F_r(X)$ is nonzero, so we deduce that the tower $\{F_r(X)\}$ is not pro-zero, in contradiction to what was established above.
nodes.statement_short: Show pointwise pro-vanishing via Mittag--Leffler (Emmanouil); then a coproduct of counterexamples gives a contradiction.

nodes.name: Pointwise pro-vanishing
nodes.statement: First we show the weaker claim that for all $X\in\mathcal{C}$, the tower $\{F_r(X)\}_r$ of abelian groups is pro-zero. Set $M_r = F_r(X)$ for brevity. From the hypothesis we find that an infinite direct sum of copies of the tower $\{M_r\}_r$ has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$; thus \cite[Cor.~6]{Emmanouil} implies that $\{M_r\}_r$ is Mittag--Leffler, i.e., for each $r$, the descending sequence $\{\mathrm{im}(M_s \to M_r)\}_{s \geq r}$ of submodules of $M_r$ stabilizes. If this stable submodule were nonzero for some $r$, we would deduce the existence of a nonzero element of $\varprojlim_s M_s$, contradicting the hypothesis. Thus the stable value is $0$ for all $r$, which exactly means that $\{M_r\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Each tower $\{F_r(X)\}$ is pro-zero.

nodes.name: Mittag--Leffler
nodes.statement: Set $M_r = F_r(X)$ for brevity. From the hypothesis we find that an infinite direct sum of copies of the tower $\{M_r\}_r$ has vanishing $\varprojlim^1$; thus \cite[Cor.~6]{Emmanouil} implies that $\{M_r\}_r$ is Mittag--Leffler, i.e., for each $r$, the descending sequence $\{\mathrm{im}(M_s \to M_r)\}_{s \geq r}$ of submodules of $M_r$ stabilizes.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing $\varprojlim^1$ of a sum of copies gives Mittag--Leffler (Emmanouil).

nodes.name: Stable images vanish
nodes.statement: If this stable submodule were nonzero for some $r$, we would deduce the existence of a nonzero element of $\varprojlim_s M_s$, contradicting the hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: A nonzero stable image would give a nonzero limit element.

nodes.name: Conclude pro-zero
nodes.statement: Thus the stable value is $0$ for all $r$, which exactly means that $\{M_r\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Stable images vanish, so the tower is pro-zero.

nodes.name: Assume not pro-zero
nodes.statement: Now, suppose the claim of the lemma does not hold, i.e., that $\{F_r\}_r$ is not pro-zero. Then for each $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $s>r$, we can find an $Y\in\mathcal{C}$ such that $F_s(Y)\rightarrow F_r(Y)$ is nonzero.
nodes.statement_short: Choose witnesses $Y$ for each pair $s>r$.

nodes.name: Coproduct counterexample
nodes.statement: Let $X$ denote the coproduct over all pairs $s>r$ of a choice of such a $Y$. Then for every $s>r$ the map $F_s(X)\rightarrow F_r(X)$ is nonzero, so we deduce that the tower $\{F_r(X)\}$ is not pro-zero, in contradiction to what was established above.
nodes.statement_short: The coproduct of witnesses violates the pointwise statement.

nodes.name: Pro-vanishing criterion for towers of spectrum-valued functors
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an $\infty$-category admitting countable coproducts, and consider a tower of functors $\mathcal{C}\rightarrow \operatorname{Sp}$, say $\ldots \rightarrow F_r\rightarrow F_{r-1}\ldots \rightarrow F_1$. Suppose that: \begin{enumerate} \item For each $X\in\mathcal{C}$ we have $\varprojlim_r F_r(X) = 0$. \item For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts. \item The homotopy groups of each $F_r(X)$ are zero outside some fixed interval $[a,b]$, independent of $X$ and $r$. \end{enumerate} Then the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero, i.e.\ it is zero as an object of $\operatorname{Pro}(\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal{C},\operatorname{Sp}))$.
assumptions: For each $r\in\mathbb{N}$, the functor $F_r$ commutes with countable coproducts.
The homotopy groups of each $F_r(X)$ are zero outside some fixed interval $[a,b]$, independent of $X$ and $r$.
conclusions: the tower $\{F_r\}_{r \geq 1}$ is pro-zero
nodes.label: invlim02

nodes.name: Proof of Pro-vanishing criterion for towers of spectrum-valued functors
nodes.statement: The Milnor sequence and induction up the Postnikov tower show that (1) implies $\varprojlim_r \pi_i F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r \pi_i F_r(X) = 0$ for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$. Since $\pi_i$ commutes with coproducts, we can apply the previous lemma to $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ and conclude that each tower $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero. Thus each Postnikov section of $\{F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero, and therefore so is $\{F_r\}_r$ itself, by devissage up the (finite) Postnikov tower.
nodes.statement_short: Milnor sequence and Postnikov induction reduce to homotopy groups, where the previous lemma applies.

nodes.name: Vanishing on homotopy
nodes.statement: The Milnor sequence and induction up the Postnikov tower show that (1) implies $\varprojlim_r \pi_i F_r(X) = \varprojlim^1_r \pi_i F_r(X) = 0$ for all $i\in\mathbb{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Limits and $\varprojlim^1$ of homotopy groups vanish.

nodes.name: Apply previous lemma
nodes.statement: Since $\pi_i$ commutes with coproducts, we can apply the previous lemma to $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ and conclude that each tower $\{\pi_i F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Each $\{\pi_iF_r\}$ is pro-zero.

nodes.name: D\'evissage
nodes.statement: Thus each Postnikov section of $\{F_r\}_r$ is pro-zero, and therefore so is $\{F_r\}_r$ itself, by devissage up the (finite) Postnikov tower.
nodes.statement_short: Finite Postnikov towers give pro-vanishing of $\{F_r\}$.

nodes.name: Pro-constancy of the $\mathrm{TC}^r$ tower modulo $p$
nodes.statement: Fix an integer $k$. Then the tower of objects of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0},\operatorname{Sp})$ given by $ \left\{ \tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p)\right\}_{r}$ is pro-constant with value $\tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}(-)/p)$.
conclusions: the tower of objects of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0},\operatorname{Sp})$ given by $ \left\{ \tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p)\right\}_{r}$ is pro-constant with value $\tau_{\leq k}(\mathrm{TC}(-)/p)$
nodes.label: prop_pro_constant

nodes.name: Proof of Pro-constancy of the $\mathrm{TC}^r$ tower modulo $p$
nodes.statement: Setting $F_{r}(X) \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} \tau_{\leq k+1}\mathrm{cofib}( \mathrm{TC}(X)/p \to \mathrm{TC}^r(X)/p)$, we will show that the tower $\{F_{r}(-)\}_r$ is pro-zero. As $k$ varies, this shows that the map $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(-)/p\right\} \to \left\{\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p\right\}_r$ is a pro-isomorphism on each homotopy group in degrees $\leq k$ (in the pro-category of functors $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Ab}$), which is enough to conclude. Certainly $\varprojlim_r F_{r}(X) = 0$, and $F_r$ commutes with arbitrary coproducts by Theorem~\ref{TCcommutes}, so the desired claim follows from Lemma~\ref{invlim02}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the pro-vanishing lemma to truncated cofibers of $\mathrm{TC}/p\to\mathrm{TC}^r/p$, using cocontinuity of TC/p.

nodes.name: Define truncated cofibers
nodes.statement: Setting $F_{r}(X) \stackrel{\mathrm{def}}{=} \tau_{\leq k+1}\mathrm{cofib}( \mathrm{TC}(X)/p \to \mathrm{TC}^r(X)/p)$, we will show that the tower $\{F_{r}(-)\}_r$ is pro-zero.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $F_r$ and reduce to showing it is pro-zero.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: As $k$ varies, this shows that the map $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(-)/p\right\} \to \left\{\mathrm{TC}^r(-)/p\right\}_r$ is a pro-isomorphism on each homotopy group in degrees $\leq k$ (in the pro-category of functors $\mathrm{CycSp}_{\geq 0} \to \mathrm{Ab}$), which is enough to conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Pro-vanishing gives pro-isomorphisms on homotopy groups.

nodes.name: Apply pro-vanishing lemma
nodes.statement: Certainly $\varprojlim_r F_{r}(X) = 0$, and $F_r$ commutes with arbitrary coproducts by Theorem~\ref{TCcommutes}, so the desired claim follows from Lemma~\ref{invlim02}.
nodes.statement_short: Cocontinuity of TC/p and the pro-vanishing lemma.

nodes.name: Differential forms $\Omega^n_R$ and de Rham complex $\Omega^\ast_R$
nodes.statement: We let $\Omega^n_R$ denote the $n$-forms of $R$ (over $\mathbb{F}_p$) and let $\Omega_R^{\ast}$ denote the algebraic de Rham complex of $R$.

nodes.name: Inverse Cartier operator
nodes.statement: The \emph{inverse Cartier operator} $C^{-1}: \Omega^n_R \to H^n(\Omega^{\ast}_R) \subset \Omega^n_R/d \Omega^{n-1}_R$ is the multiplicative operator uniquely characterized by the formulas \( C^{-1}(a) = a^p, \quad C^{-1}(db) = b^{p-1} db, \) for $a, b \in R$. See \cite{Cartier1957}, also \cite[Prop.~3.3.4]{BLM}, for a construction of this map.
nodes.label: cartier

nodes.name: Ind-smooth algebra and Cartier isomorphism
nodes.statement: It has image in the cohomology of the de Rham complex; if we further assume that $R$ is ind-smooth, i.e., can be written as a filtered colimit of smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras\footnote{Since smooth algebras are finitely presented, it follows that the category of ind-smooth algebras indeed identifies with $\operatorname{Ind}$ of the category of smooth algebras.}, then $C^{-1}$ provides a natural (Frobenius semi-linear) isomorphism between $\Omega^n_R$ and $H^n( \Omega_R^{\ast})$ by the classical \emph{Cartier isomorphism}, cf.~\cite[Th.~7.2]{Katz70}.
nodes.statement_short: Ind-smooth means a filtered colimit of smooth algebras; for these $C^{-1}$ is an isomorphism onto de Rham cohomology.

nodes.name: de Rham--Witt complex
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra. For $r\ge 1$, we denote as usual by \[W_r(R)\xrightarrow{d}W_r\Omega^1_R\xrightarrow{d}W_r\Omega^2_R\xrightarrow{d}\cdots\] the classical de Rham--Witt complex (more precisely, differential graded algebras) of Bloch--Deligne--Illusie \cite{illusie-derham-witt}; this is the usual de Rham complex $\Omega^\bullet_R$ in the case $r=1$. We recall that the individual de Rham--Witt groups are equipped with Restriction and Frobenius maps $R,F:W_r\Omega^n_R\to W_{r-1}\Omega^n_R$. We let $W \Omega_R^{\ast}$ denote the inverse limit of the tower $\left\{W_r \Omega^{\ast}_R\right\}$ under the Restriction maps.
nodes.label: dRW1

nodes.name: Frobenius on de Rham--Witt lifts the inverse Cartier operator
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ W\Omega_R^{\ast} \ar[d] \ar[r]^F & W \Omega_R^{\ast} \ar[d] \\ \Omega_R^{\ast} \ar[r]^-{C^{-1}} & \Omega_R^{\ast}/d \Omega^{\ast-1}_R. }

nodes.name: Hesselholt's HKR theorem for TR
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. Then, for each $s\ge1$, we have an isomorphism of graded rings \begin{equation} \mathrm{TR}^s_*(R; p) \simeq W_s \Omega^{\ast}_R \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}/p^s} \mathbb{Z}/p^s [ \sigma_s], \quad |\sigma_s| = 2. \end{equation} The Restriction maps are determined by the Restriction maps on the de Rham--Witt complex and send $\sigma_s \mapsto p \sigma_{s-1}$. Therefore, we have an isomorphism \begin{equation} \mathrm{TR}_*(R; p) \simeq W \Omega^{\ast}_R, \end{equation} and the $F$ map on $\mathrm{TR}(R; p)$ induces the $F$ map on $W \Omega_R^{\ast}$.
nodes.statement_short: For smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, $\mathrm{TR}$ is computed by the de Rham--Witt complex.
conclusions: for each $s\ge1$, we have an isomorphism of graded rings
\mathrm{TR}_*(R; p) \simeq W \Omega^{\ast}_R

nodes.name: HKR isomorphism for $\mathrm{TR}^s$
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TR}^s_*(R; p) \simeq W_s \Omega^{\ast}_R \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}/p^s} \mathbb{Z}/p^s [ \sigma_s], \quad |\sigma_s| = 2.
nodes.label: HHKR1

nodes.name: HKR isomorphism for TR
nodes.statement: \mathrm{TR}_*(R; p) \simeq W \Omega^{\ast}_R,
nodes.label: HHKR2

nodes.name: TC/p commutes with filtered colimits of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
nodes.statement: The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}_{/\mathbb F_p}\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $R\mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$ commutes with filtered colimits.
conclusions: The functor $\operatorname{CAlg}_{/\mathbb F_p}\to\mathrm{Sp}$, $R\mapsto \mathrm{TC}(R)/p$ commutes with filtered colimits

nodes.name: Proof of TC/p commutes with filtered colimits of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ be a filtered colimit of $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. By functorially picking simplicial resolutions of all the terms by ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebras, and recalling that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ commutes with geometric realizations of rings, we reduce to the case in which all the $R_i$ (hence also $R$ itself) are ind-smooth over $\mathbb F_p$. Next we use Hesselholt's HKR theorem. Since each $\mathrm{TR}^s(-;p)$ commutes with filtered colimits (induction on (\ref{keyformulaclassical})), as does $W_s\Omega^n_{-}$, the formula \eqref{HHKR1} remains valid for ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. By taking the inverse limit over $s$, we deduce that $\pi_*(\mathrm{TR}(R;p)) \simeq W\Omega_R^*$ for any ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$, i.e., \eqref{HHKR2} is valid in the ind-smooth case as well. Note here that each $W\Omega_R^n$ is $p$-torsion-free, by a basic property of the de Rham--Witt complex for smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras \cite[Cor.~I.3.6]{illusie-derham-witt} which can easily be extended to the ind-smooth case as it derives from the stronger assertion that each Restriction map $W_s \Omega_R^{\ast} \to W_{s-1} \Omega_R^{\ast}$ annihilates every element $x \in W_s \Omega_R^{\ast}$ with $px = 0$. As a result, we also conclude that $\pi_* ( \mathrm{TR}(R; p)/p) \simeq W \Omega_R^{\ast}/p$. Taking fixed points for the Frobenius, we find that $\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)$ fits into an exact sequence \[W\Omega^{n+1}_R/p\xrightarrow{F-1}W\Omega^{n+1}_R/p\longrightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p)\longrightarrow W\Omega^{n}_R/p\xrightarrow{F-1}W\Omega^{n}_R/p,\] and similarly for each $R_i$. To complete the proof it is enough to show, for each $n\ge0$, that the kernel and cokernel of $F-1:W\Omega^{n}_-/p\to W\Omega^{n}_-/p$ commutes with our filtered colimit $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$; we stress that $W\Omega^{n}_-/p$ does not commute with filtered colimits. For any ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$, consider the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[r]^{F-1}\ar[d] & W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[d]\\ \Omega^n_R\ar[r]_{C^{-1}-1}&\Omega^n_R/d\Omega^{n-1}_R }. \end{equation} Here $C^{-1}$ is the inverse Cartier operator. To complete the proof we will show that the two horizontal arrows have isomorphic kernels (resp.\ cokernels), i.e., the square is both cartesian and cocartesian. To see this, it suffices to show that the map induced between the kernels of the vertical maps (which are surjective) is an isomorphism. The kernel of the map $W \Omega^n_R \to \Omega^n_R$ is generated by the images of $V, dV$ by \cite[Proposition I.3.18]{illusie-derham-witt}. Note that the citation is for smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, but the statement clearly passes to an ind-smooth algebra as the terms $W_s \Omega^n_{-}$ commute with filtered colimits and $W \Omega^n_{-} = \varprojlim W_s \Omega^n_{-}$. It follows that the kernel of the first vertical map in \eqref{thisdiag} is spanned by the images of $V, dV$ while the kernel of the second vertical map is spanned by the images of $V, d$. Thus, we need to show that the map \begin{equation} F - 1: \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p\xrightarrow{V+dV} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \to \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p \xrightarrow{V+d} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \end{equation} is an isomorphism. First, we show that $F-1$ is surjective. We record the following identities in $W \Omega_R^n/p$, \[(F-1)V=-V,\qquad (F-1)d\sum_{i>0}V^i=d;\] using it, we see immediately that $F - 1$ is surjective in \eqref{mapFminusone}. To see injectivity, we will use an important property of the de Rham--Witt complex: the image of $F$ on $W \Omega_R^n$ consists precisely of those elements $w$ with $dw$ divisible by $p$, thanks to \cite[(I.3.21.1.5)]{illusie-derham-witt}. Again, the reference is stated in the smooth case, but it also passes to the ind-smooth case;\footnote{Since the passage to the ind-smooth case is not completely immediate, we provide the argument. Firstly, the quasi-isomorphisms $W_s \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^{\bullet}$ for $s\ge1$ in the smooth case \cite[Corol.~I.3.15]{illusie-derham-witt} extend at once to the ind-smooth case, and taking the limit then shows $W \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^\bullet$ (to take the limit recall again that the $p$-torsion in $W_s\Omega^n_R$ is annihilated by $R:W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_R$). Secondly, the identity $\ker(d \colon \Omega^n_R\to\Omega^{n+1}_R)=\mathrm{Im}( F \colon W_2\Omega^n_R\to \Omega^n_R)$ also extends at once from the smooth \cite[Prop.~I.3.21]{illusie-derham-witt} to the ind-smooth case. Therefore, given $w\in W\Omega^n_R$ satisfying $dw\in pW\Omega^n_R$, we may write $w=Fx+y$ for some $x,y\in W\Omega^n_R$ such that $y$ vanishes in $\Omega^n_R$. But then $dy=dw-pFdx\in pW\Omega^n_R$, so $y$ defines a class in $H^n(W\Omega^\bullet/p)$ which vanishes in $H^n(\Omega^\bullet_R)$; by the first claim, we deduce that the initial class was zero, in other words that $y=dz+pz'$ for some $z\in W\Omega^{n-1}_R$, $z'\in W\Omega^n_R$. So $w= Fx+FdVz+FVz'$, as required.} for more on this point cf.~\cite[Sec.~2]{BLM}. Suppose $x \in W \Omega^n_R$ can be written as $x = Vy + dVz$ and $(F -1 )x $ is divisible by $p$; we show that $x $ is divisible by $p$ in $ W \Omega^n_R$. This will hold if $y, z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$. First, $-dx \equiv d((F-1) x)$ modulo $p$, so $dx$ is divisible by $p$. It follows that $d Vy$, and hence $dy = FdVy$ is divisible by $p$, so that $y$ belongs to the image of $F$. In particular, modulo $p$, we have $x \equiv dV z$ and $(F-1) d Vz = d (z - Vz)$ is divisible by $p$. Therefore, $z - Vz$ belongs to the image of $F$. Since the operator $V$ is topologically nilpotent on $W \Omega^n_R$, we find that $(1 - V)$ is invertible and $z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$. Therefore, $x$ is divisible by $p$ as desired.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to ind-smooth algebras and use Hesselholt's HKR to express $\pi_*\mathrm{TC}/p$ via $F-1$ on $W\Omega/p$. The key step compares $F-1$ with $C^{-1}-1$ and shows $F-1$ is bijective on images of $V,dV$.

nodes.statement: Let $R=\operatorname{colim}_iR_i$ be a filtered colimit of $\mathbb F_p$-algebras. nodes.name: Comparison square with $C^{-1}-1$
nodes.statement: For any ind-smooth $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$, consider the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[r]^{F-1}\ar[d] & W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[d]\\ \Omega^n_R\ar[r]_{C^{-1}-1}&\Omega^n_R/d\Omega^{n-1}_R }. \end{equation} Here $C^{-1}$ is the inverse Cartier operator. nodes.statement_short: Compare $F-1$ with $C^{-1}-1$ on forms.

nodes.name: Comparison of $F-1$ with $C^{-1}-1$
nodes.statement: \xymatrix{ W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[r]^{F-1}\ar[d] & W\Omega^{n}_R/p\ar[d]\\ \Omega^n_R\ar[r]_{C^{-1}-1}&\Omega^n_R/d\Omega^{n-1}_R }.
nodes.label: thisdiag

nodes.name: Reduce to kernels of vertical maps
nodes.statement: To see this, it suffices to show that the map induced between the kernels of the vertical maps (which are surjective) is an isomorphism. The kernel of the map $W \Omega^n_R \to \Omega^n_R$ is generated by the images of $V, dV$ by \cite[Proposition I.3.18]{illusie-derham-witt}. Note that the citation is for smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, but the statement clearly passes to an ind-smooth algebra as the terms $W_s \Omega^n_{-}$ commute with filtered colimits and $W \Omega^n_{-} = \varprojlim W_s \Omega^n_{-}$. It follows that the kernel of the first vertical map in \eqref{thisdiag} is spanned by the images of $V, dV$ while the kernel of the second vertical map is spanned by the images of $V, d$.
nodes.statement_short: Kernels are spanned by images of $V,dV$ and $V,d$.

nodes.name: Reduced statement
nodes.statement: Thus, we need to show that the map \begin{equation} F - 1: \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p\xrightarrow{V+dV} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \to \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p \xrightarrow{V+d} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \end{equation} is an isomorphism.
nodes.statement_short: Show $F-1$ is an isomorphism between these images.

nodes.name: $F-1$ on images of $V$ and $dV$
nodes.statement: F - 1: \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p\xrightarrow{V+dV} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right) \to \mathrm{im}\left(W \Omega^n_{R}/p\oplus W \Omega^{n-1}_{R}/p \xrightarrow{V+d} W \Omega^n_{R}/p\right)
nodes.label: mapFminusone

nodes.name: Surjectivity
nodes.statement: First, we show that $F-1$ is surjective. We record the following identities in $W \Omega_R^n/p$, \[(F-1)V=-V,\qquad (F-1)d\sum_{i>0}V^i=d;\] using it, we see immediately that $F - 1$ is surjective in \eqref{mapFminusone}.

Firstly, the quasi-isomorphisms $W_s \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^{\bullet}$ for $s\ge1$ in the smooth case \cite[Corol.~I.3.15]{illusie-derham-witt} extend at once to the ind-smooth case, and taking the limit then shows $W \Omega_R^\bullet/p\simeq \Omega_R^\bullet$ (to take the limit recall again that the $p$-torsion in $W_s\Omega^n_R$ is annihilated by $R:W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_R$). So $w= Fx+FdVz+FVz'$, as required.} for more on this point cf.~\cite[Sec.~2]{BLM}.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the image of $F$ consists of forms with $dw$ divisible by $p$.

nodes.name: Injectivity
nodes.statement: Suppose $x \in W \Omega^n_R$ can be written as $x = Vy + dVz$ and $(F -1 )x $ is divisible by $p$; we show that $x $ is divisible by $p$ in $ W \Omega^n_R$. This will hold if $y, z \in \mathrm{im}(F)$. First, $-dx \equiv d((F-1) x)$ modulo $p$, so $dx$ is divisible by $p$. It follows that $d Vy$, and hence $dy = FdVy$ is divisible by $p$, so that $y$ belongs to the image of $F$.
