nodes.name: Vector space $V$
nodes.statement: Let $V$ be a vector space over a field $k$.

nodes.name: Weight of a 2-form
nodes.statement: Given a 2-form $\omega \in \bigwedge^2 V$, we define the \emph{weight} of $\omega$ to be the minimal $n$ such that there exist elements $\left\{x_i, y_i|1 \leq i \leq n\right\} \subset V$ such that $\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n x_i \wedge y_i$.

nodes.name: Weight of a sum of wedges of independent vectors
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{u_1, \dots, u_n, v_1, \dots, v_n\right\}$ be linearly independent in $V$. Then the form $\sum_{i=1}^n u_i \wedge v_i$ has weight $n$.
assumptions: $\left\{u_1, \dots, u_n, v_1, \dots, v_n\right\}$ be linearly independent in $V$
conclusions: the form $\sum_{i=1}^n u_i \wedge v_i$ has weight $n$
nodes.label: linalg

nodes.name: Proof of Weight of a sum of wedges of independent vectors
nodes.statement: Recall that we have an \emph{interior product} $V^{\vee} \otimes \bigwedge^2 V \to V$ given by $v \otimes (x \wedge y) \mapsto \left \langle v, x\right\rangle y - \left \langle v, y\right\rangle x$. Given $\omega \in \bigwedge^2 V$, we obtain a map $f_\omega: V^{\vee} \to V$. If $\omega$ has weight $w$, then the rank of $f_{\omega}$ is at most $2w$. Completing $\left\{u_1,\dots, u_n, v_1, \dots, v_n\right\}$ to a basis of $V$ and forming the dual basis, one now sees that the rank of $f_{\omega_0}$ for $\omega_0 = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \wedge v_i$ is $2n$; together, this implies the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the rank of the contraction map $V^\vee\to V$ by twice the weight.

nodes.name: Contraction map
nodes.statement: Recall that we have an \emph{interior product} $V^{\vee} \otimes \bigwedge^2 V \to V$ given by $v \otimes (x \wedge y) \mapsto \left \langle v, x\right\rangle y - \left \langle v, y\right\rangle x$. Given $\omega \in \bigwedge^2 V$, we obtain a map $f_\omega: V^{\vee} \to V$.
nodes.statement_short: Interior product gives $f_\omega$.

nodes.name: Rank bound
nodes.statement: If $\omega$ has weight $w$, then the rank of $f_{\omega}$ is at most $2w$.
nodes.statement_short: Rank at most $2w$.

nodes.name: Rank of $\omega_0$
nodes.statement: Completing $\left\{u_1,\dots, u_n, v_1, \dots, v_n\right\}$ to a basis of $V$ and forming the dual basis, one now sees that the rank of $f_{\omega_0}$ for $\omega_0 = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i \wedge v_i$ is $2n$; together, this implies the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Rank equals $2n$.

nodes.name: $p$-adic continuity of K-theory
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. We say that $K$-theory is \emph{$p$-adically continuous} for $R$ if the map of spectra $K(R) \to \varprojlim_i K(R/p^iR)$ is an equivalence modulo $p$.

nodes.name: Geisser--Hesselholt $p$-adic continuity
nodes.statement: If $R$ is a local ring which is $p$-torsion-free and henselian along $(p)$, then $K$-theory is $p$-adically continuous at $R$. Moreover, the map $K(R)/p \to \left\{ K(R/p^iR)/p\right\}_{i \geq 1}$ induces an isomorphism of pro abelian groups upon applying $\pi_j$ for any $j$.
assumptions: $R$ is a local ring which is $p$-torsion-free and henselian along $(p)$
conclusions: $K$-theory is $p$-adically continuous at $R$
the map $K(R)/p \to \left\{ K(R/p^iR)/p\right\}_{i \geq 1}$ induces an isomorphism of pro abelian groups upon applying $\pi_j$ for any $j$
nodes.label: GHcontinuity

nodes.name: $K^{\mathrm{inv}}$ of $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra
nodes.statement: The functors $K, \mathrm{TC}$ are defined not only for ordinary rings $R$, but more generally for arbitrary $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra $R$. For such $R$, we define $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)$ similarly, as the fiber of the cyclotomic trace $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$.

nodes.name: Dundas--Goodwillie--McCarthy theorem for connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebras
nodes.statement: Part of the theorem of Dundas--Goodwillie--McCarthy \cite{dgm} states that if $R$ is a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra, then the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(\pi_0 R)$ is an equivalence.
conclusions: the map $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) \to K^{\mathrm{inv}}(\pi_0 R)$ is an equivalence

nodes.name: Nilpotent and quickly converging towers of abelian groups
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{A_i\right\}_{i \geq 1}$ be a tower of abelian groups. We say that the tower is \emph{nilpotent} if there exists $N> 0$ such that all the maps $A_{i+N} \to A_i$ are zero. We say that the tower is \emph{quickly converging} if there exists $r \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ such that the tower $\{\mathrm{im}(A_{i+r} \to A_i)\}_{i\ge1}$ is eventually constant. This is stronger than the Mittag--Leffler condition.
nodes.label: quickconvab

nodes.name: Quickly converging towers form an abelian subcategory
nodes.statement: By \cite[Lemma 3.10]{Mthick}, it follows that the collection of towers of abelian groups which are quickly converging forms an abelian subcategory of the category of towers which is closed under extensions.
conclusions: the collection of towers of abelian groups which are quickly converging forms an abelian subcategory of the category of towers which is closed under extensions

nodes.name: Comparison of a quickly converging tower with its limit
nodes.statement: It thus follows that if $\left\{A_i\right\}$ is a quickly converging tower and $A$ is the inverse limit, then the kernel and cokernel of the map of towers $\left\{A\right\} \to \left\{A_i\right\}$ are both nilpotent.
assumptions: $\left\{A_i\right\}$ is a quickly converging tower and $A$ is the inverse limit
conclusions: the kernel and cokernel of the map of towers $\left\{A\right\} \to \left\{A_i\right\}$ are both nilpotent

nodes.name: Quickly converging towers are generated by constant and nilpotent towers
nodes.statement: In particular, the category of quickly converging towers is the smallest abelian subcategory containing the nilpotent towers and the constant towers which is closed under extensions.
conclusions: the category of quickly converging towers is the smallest abelian subcategory containing the nilpotent towers and the constant towers which is closed under extensions

nodes.name: Nilpotent and quickly converging towers of spectra
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}_{i \geq 1}$ be a tower in $\mathrm{Sp}$, i.e., $\{X_i\}_{i\ge1}\in\operatorname{Tow}(\mathrm{Sp}):=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbb N^\sub{op},\mathrm{Sp})$. We say that the tower is \emph{nilpotent} if there exists $N> 0$ such that all the maps $X_{i+N} \to X_i$ are nullhomotopic. The collection of nilpotent towers forms a thick subcategory of the stable $\infty$-category $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathrm{Sp})$. We say that a tower $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is \emph{quickly converging} if the cofiber of the map of towers $\left\{X\right\} \to \left\{X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, where $X:=\varprojlim_iX_i$, or equivalently if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ lies in the smallest thick subcategory of towers containing the constant towers and the nilpotent towers.

nodes.name: Quick convergence via homotopy groups
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}_{i\ge1}$ be a tower in $\mathrm{Sp}$. If $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is quickly converging, the tower $\left\{\pi_j X_i\right\}$ of abelian groups is quickly converging for each $j$. The converse holds if we suppose that each $X_i$ has homotopy groups concentrated in the fixed range $[a,b]$.
assumptions: each $X_i$ has homotopy groups concentrated in the fixed range $[a,b]$
conclusions: the tower $\left\{\pi_j X_i\right\}$ of abelian groups is quickly converging for each $j$
The converse holds
the tower $\left\{\pi_j X_i\right\}$ of abelian groups is quickly converging for each $j$

assumptions: each $X_i$ has homotopy groups concentrated in the fixed range $[a,b]$
conclusions: The converse holds

nodes.name: Proof of Quick convergence via homotopy groups
nodes.statement: It follows from \cite[Lemma 3.11]{Mthick} that if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is quickly converging, then the towers of homotopy groups are quickly converging. Indeed, if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent or constant, then the tower of homotopy groups is clearly quickly converging, and the referenced result shows that the condition on homotopy groups is stable in cofiber sequences of towers. For the converse direction, a d\'evissage reduces to the case where $a= b$. In this case, it follows from the paragraph following Definition~\ref{quickconvab}: that is, quickly convergent towers of abelian groups are built up from constant and nilpotent towers.
nodes.statement_short: Cite Mathew's lemma on cofiber sequences; d\'evissage for the converse.

nodes.name: Forward direction
nodes.statement: It follows from \cite[Lemma 3.11]{Mthick} that if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is quickly converging, then the towers of homotopy groups are quickly converging. Indeed, if $\left\{X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent or constant, then the tower of homotopy groups is clearly quickly converging, and the referenced result shows that the condition on homotopy groups is stable in cofiber sequences of towers.
nodes.statement_short: Mathew's lemma.

nodes.name: Converse
nodes.statement: For the converse direction, a d\'evissage reduces to the case where $a= b$. In this case, it follows from the paragraph following Definition~\ref{quickconvab}: that is, quickly convergent towers of abelian groups are built up from constant and nilpotent towers.
nodes.statement_short: D\'evissage to one degree.

nodes.name: Almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers
nodes.statement: We say that a tower $\left\{X_i\right\}$ of spectra is \emph{almost nilpotent} if for each $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, the truncated tower $\left\{\tau_{\leq n} X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, or equivalently if each tower $\left\{\pi_n (X_i)\right\}$ of abelian groups is nilpotent. We say that a tower is \emph{almost quickly converging} if for each $n$, the tower $\left\{\tau_{\leq n} X_i\right\}$ is quickly converging. If the tower is uniformly bounded below, then it is almost quickly converging if and only if each tower $\left\{\pi_n (X_i)\right\}$ of abelian groups is quickly convergent.

nodes.name: Proof of thickness of almost nilpotent towers
nodes.statement: The following then is a direct consequence of \cite[Lemma 3.11]{Mthick}.
nodes.statement_short: Direct consequence of Mathew's Lemma 3.11.

nodes.name: Thickness of almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers
nodes.statement: The almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers form thick subcategories of $\mathrm{Tow}( \mathrm{Sp})$ including the nilpotent and quickly converging towers respectively.
conclusions: The almost nilpotent and almost quickly converging towers form thick subcategories of $\mathrm{Tow}( \mathrm{Sp})$ including the nilpotent and quickly converging towers respectively

nodes.name: Geometric realizations of almost quickly converging towers
nodes.statement: Let $X_{\bullet, \ast}$ be a simplicial object in the $\infty$-category of towers of connective spectra. Suppose each tower $\dots \to X_{j,2} \to X_{j, 1}$ is almost quickly convergent, with limit $X_j$. Then the geometric realization $\dots \to |X_{\bullet, 2}| \to |X_{\bullet, 1}|$ is almost quickly converging and has limit $\vert X_\bullet \vert$ via the natural comparison map.
assumptions: $X_{\bullet, \ast}$ be a simplicial object in the $\infty$-category of towers of connective spectra
each tower $\dots \to X_{j,2} \to X_{j, 1}$ is almost quickly convergent, with limit $X_j$
conclusions: the geometric realization $\dots \to |X_{\bullet, 2}| \to |X_{\bullet, 1}|$ is almost quickly converging and has limit $\vert X_\bullet \vert$ via the natural comparison map
nodes.label: simplicialalmostquickconv

nodes.name: Proof of Geometric realizations of almost quickly converging towers
nodes.statement: This follows from approximating the geometric realization with an $n$-skeletal geometric realization in any range of degrees.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate by finite skeletal realizations.

nodes.name: TC/p preserves almost quick convergence
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}$ be a tower in $\mathrm{CycSp}_{ \geq 0}$. Suppose that the underlying tower of spectra $\left\{X_i/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging. Then the tower of spectra $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(X_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging.
assumptions: the underlying tower of spectra $\left\{X_i/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging
conclusions: the tower of spectra $\left\{\mathrm{TC}(X_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging
nodes.label: TCalmostquickconv

nodes.name: Proof of TC/p preserves almost quick convergence
nodes.statement: This follows in a similar fashion as Proposition~\ref{strong:finiteness}. See also Remark \ref{TCinvlim} for the identification of the inverse limit of the above tower in $\mathrm{CycSp}$.
nodes.statement_short: As for the approximation of TC/p by homotopy orbits.

nodes.name: Smash products of almost quickly converging towers
nodes.statement: Let $\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ be two towers of connective spectra. If $\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ are almost quickly converging with inverse limits $X$ and $Y$, then $\left\{X_i\otimes Y_i\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with inverse limit $X\otimes Y$.
assumptions: $\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ be two towers of connective spectra
$\left\{X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{Y_i\right\}$ are almost quickly converging with inverse limits $X$ and $Y$
conclusions: $\left\{X_i\otimes Y_i\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with inverse limit $X\otimes Y$
nodes.label: transfernilp

nodes.name: Proof of Smash products of almost quickly converging towers
nodes.statement: Note that $\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i) \simeq \tau_{\leq m} ( \tau_{\leq m} X_i \otimes Y_i)$. So if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, then so is $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i)\right\}$, and the limit is zero. Symmetrically, we get the same if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}Y_i\right\}$ is nilpotent. On the other hand, if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} Y_i\right\}$ are both constant, we see that $\tau_{\leq m} (X_i\otimes Y_i)$ is constant, and the map from $X\otimes Y$ to the limit is an isomorphism degrees $\leq m-1$. A thick subcategory argument lets us conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Truncation reduces to nilpotent or constant towers; thick subcategory argument.

nodes.name: Truncation identity
nodes.statement: Note that $\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i) \simeq \tau_{\leq m} ( \tau_{\leq m} X_i \otimes Y_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Truncate the factors.

nodes.name: Nilpotent factor
nodes.statement: So if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} X_i\right\}$ is nilpotent, then so is $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}( X_i \otimes Y_i)\right\}$, and the limit is zero. Symmetrically, we get the same if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}Y_i\right\}$ is nilpotent.
nodes.statement_short: Product is nilpotent.

nodes.name: Constant factors
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if $\left\{\tau_{\leq m}X_i\right\}$ and $\left\{\tau_{\leq m} Y_i\right\}$ are both constant, we see that $\tau_{\leq m} (X_i\otimes Y_i)$ is constant, and the map from $X\otimes Y$ to the limit is an isomorphism degrees $\leq m-1$.
nodes.statement_short: Product constant with correct limit.

nodes.name: Thick subcategory
nodes.statement: A thick subcategory argument lets us conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude.

nodes.name: Continuity of TC modulo $p$ for towers of ring spectra
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\{R_i\}_{i\ge1}$ is a tower of connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra, and $R$ is another connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectrum with a comparison map $R\rightarrow \varprojlim_i R_i$. If this comparison map is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower of spectra $\{R_i/p\}$ is almost quickly converging, then the comparison map $$\mathrm{TC}(R)\rightarrow\varprojlim_i \mathrm{TC}(R_i)$$ is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower $\{\mathrm{TC}(R_i)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging.
assumptions: $\{R_i\}_{i\ge1}$ is a tower of connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectra, and $R$ is another connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-ring spectrum with a comparison map $R\rightarrow \varprojlim_i R_i$
this comparison map is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower of spectra $\{R_i/p\}$ is almost quickly converging
conclusions: is an equivalence modulo $p$ and the tower $\{\mathrm{TC}(R_i)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging
nodes.label: THHmodp

nodes.name: Proof of Continuity of TC modulo $p$ for towers of ring spectra
nodes.statement: Note that a tower is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ if and only if it is almost quickly converging after smashing with $X$, for any choice of spectrum $X$ generating the same thick subcategory as $S^0/p$. For example one can take $X=S^0/p\otimes S^0/p$.\footnote{This is the cone of multiplcation by $p$ on $S^0/p$, hence lies in the thick subcategory generated by $S^0/p$. For the converse, note that $p^2$ kills $S^0/p$, so $S^0/p$ is a retract of $(S^0/p \otimes S^0/p)/p$.} Keeping this in mind, an inductive application of Lemma \ref{transfernilp} shows that $\left\{(HR_i)^{\otimes n}\right\}_i$ is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ for any $n\geq 0$, and has mod~$p$ limit $(HR)^{\otimes n}/p$. Then by Lemma \ref{simplicialalmostquickconv} we deduce that $\left\{\mathrm{THH}(R_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with limit $\mathrm{THH}(R)/p$. From this, Lemma \ref{TCalmostquickconv} lets us conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Smash powers and THH preserve almost quick convergence mod $p$; then pass to TC.

nodes.name: Change of coefficients
nodes.statement: Note that a tower is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ if and only if it is almost quickly converging after smashing with $X$, for any choice of spectrum $X$ generating the same thick subcategory as $S^0/p$. For example one can take $X=S^0/p\otimes S^0/p$.\footnote{This is the cone of multiplcation by $p$ on $S^0/p$, hence lies in the thick subcategory generated by $S^0/p$. For the converse, note that $p^2$ kills $S^0/p$, so $S^0/p$ is a retract of $(S^0/p \otimes S^0/p)/p$.}
nodes.statement_short: Use $S^0/p\otimes S^0/p$.

nodes.name: Smash powers
nodes.statement: Keeping this in mind, an inductive application of Lemma \ref{transfernilp} shows that $\left\{(HR_i)^{\otimes n}\right\}_i$ is almost quickly converging modulo $p$ for any $n\geq 0$, and has mod~$p$ limit $(HR)^{\otimes n}/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Smash-product lemma.

nodes.name: THH
nodes.statement: Then by Lemma \ref{simplicialalmostquickconv} we deduce that $\left\{\mathrm{THH}(R_i)/p\right\}$ is almost quickly converging with limit $\mathrm{THH}(R)/p$.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric realization lemma.

nodes.name: TC
nodes.statement: From this, Lemma \ref{TCalmostquickconv} lets us conclude.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to TC/p.

nodes.name: $H\mathbb{Z}$-module spectra $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$
nodes.statement: We denote by $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$ the symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category of $H\mathbb{Z}$-module spectra, or equivalently the derived $\infty$-category of $\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Derived $p$-adic continuity of TC
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$. Then the map \[ \mathrm{TC}(R) \to \varprojlim_i \mathrm{TC}( R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i) \] is a $p$-adic equivalence. Moreover the tower on the right-hand-side is almost quickly converging modulo $p$.
conclusions: is a $p$-adic equivalence
the tower on the right-hand-side is almost quickly converging modulo $p$
nodes.label: TCderpcontinuous

nodes.name: Proof of Derived $p$-adic continuity of TC
nodes.statement: It suffices to remark that the transition maps in the tower of fibers $\{\operatorname{fib}(R\rightarrow R\otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z})\}_n$ identify with multiplication by $p$ maps, hence are zero modulo $p$, so that Proposition \ref{THHmodp} applies.
nodes.statement_short: The fiber tower has transition maps multiplication by $p$.

nodes.name: Derived $p$-adic continuity of K-theory
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$ such that $\pi_0(R)$ is commutative and henselian along $(p)$. Then the tower $\{K(R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}) / p\}_{i \geq 1}$ is almost quickly converging, and $$K(R)\rightarrow \varprojlim_i K(R\otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}}H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z})$$ is an equivalence modulo $p$.
assumptions: $R$ be a connective $\mathbb{E}_1$-algebra in $\mathrm{Mod}_{H\mathbb{Z}}$ such that $\pi_0(R)$ is commutative and henselian along $(p)$
conclusions: the tower $\{K(R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}) / p\}_{i \geq 1}$ is almost quickly converging
$$K(R)\rightarrow \varprojlim_i K(R\otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}}H\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z})$$ is an equivalence modulo $p$
nodes.label: derivedpadiccont

nodes.name: Proof of Derived $p$-adic continuity of K-theory
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{mainthm} we see $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R) = K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R \otimes_{H\mathbb{Z}} H\mathbb{Z}/p^i \mathbb{Z})$ for each $i$. This reduces us to the analogous result for $\mathrm{TC}$, which is Theorem~\ref{TCderpcontinuous}.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem reduces to TC continuity.

nodes.name: $p$-adic continuity of K-theory for rings henselian along $(p)$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$, and suppose the $p$-power-torsion in $R$ is bounded. Then $K$-theory is $p$-adically continuous at $R$. Moreover, the tower $\{K(R/p^iR)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging.
assumptions: $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$
conclusions: $K$-theory is $p$-adically continuous at $R$
the tower $\{K(R/p^iR)/p\}$ is almost quickly converging

nodes.name: Proof of $p$-adic continuity of K-theory for rings henselian along $(p)$
nodes.statement: The map of towers $\{HR\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}\}\rightarrow \{H(R/p^iR)\}$ has fiber $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ with transition maps multiplication by $p$. Because of the bounded $p$-power torsion hypothesis, this tower $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ is almost nilpotent modulo $p$. So we deduce $p$-adic continuity for $\mathrm{TC}$ as in Proposition \ref{TCderpcontinuous}, and then $p$-adic continuity for $K$-theory as in Proposition \ref{derivedpadiccont}.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded torsion makes the fiber tower almost nilpotent mod $p$; argue as in the derived case.

nodes.name: Fiber tower
nodes.statement: The map of towers $\{HR\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}\}\rightarrow \{H(R/p^iR)\}$ has fiber $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ with transition maps multiplication by $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Fiber is $\Sigma H(R[p^i])$ with multiplication by $p$.

nodes.name: Almost nilpotent
nodes.statement: Because of the bounded $p$-power torsion hypothesis, this tower $\{\Sigma H(R[p^i])\}$ is almost nilpotent modulo $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded torsion.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: So we deduce $p$-adic continuity for $\mathrm{TC}$ as in Proposition \ref{TCderpcontinuous}, and then $p$-adic continuity for $K$-theory as in Proposition \ref{derivedpadiccont}.
nodes.statement_short: Argue as in derived case.

nodes.name: Variant without $\mathbb{Z}$-linear structure
nodes.statement: Without assuming $\mathbb{Z}$-linear structure, one can get similar results by replacing $-\otimes_\mathbb{Z}\mathbb{Z}/p^i\mathbb{Z}$ with $-\otimes S_i$ for any reasonable tower of $E_\infty$-algebras $\left\{S_i\right\}$ of which $p$-adically approximates the sphere spectrum, for example the tower coming from the usual cosimplicial Adams resolution associated to $S^0\rightarrow H\mathbb{F}_p$.

nodes.name: Logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra. We recall the de Rham-Witt complex $\{W_r \Omega_R^{\ast}\}$ as in \cite{illusie-derham-witt} (see also Definition~\ref{dRW1}). Letting $[\cdot]:R\to W_r(R)$ denote the Teichm\"uller lift, there is a resulting group homomorphism $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:R^\times\to W_r\Omega^1_R$, $\alpha\mapsto\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha]=\tfrac{d[\alpha]}{[\alpha]}$, and more generally \[\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:R^{\times\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{R}^n,\quad \alpha_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\alpha_n\mapsto\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_n].\] When $R$ is local, the image of this map will be denoted by $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$.
nodes.statement_short: For local $R$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\mathrm{log}}$ is the image of $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on $n$-fold tensors of units.
nodes.label: definition_dRW

nodes.name: Globalization of de Rham--Witt sheaves
nodes.statement: Given an $\mathbb F_p$-scheme $X$, one defines $W_r\Omega^n_X$ to be the Zariski (or \'etale, depending on the context) sheaf obtained by sheafifying $U\mapsto W_r\Omega^n_{\mathcal O_X(U)}$. When $X=\mathrm{Spec} R$ is affine, this sheaf (in either topology) has no higher cohomology and has global sections $W_r\Omega_R^n$: this follows from flat descent and the facts that if $R\to S$ is \'etale then so is $W_r(R)\to W_r(S)$ \cite[Thm.~2.4]{vanderKallen1986} and moreover the canonical map $W_r\Omega_R^n\otimes_{W_r(R)}W_r(S)\to W_r\Omega_S^n$ is an isomorphism \cite[Prop.~1.7]{LangerZink2004}. We define $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ to be the subgroup of $W_r\Omega^n_R$ consisting of elements which can be written Zariski locally as sums of dlog forms, i.e., $H^0(\mathrm{Spec} R,-)$ of the image (as a Zariski sheaf) of \[\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\mathbb G_{m,\mathrm{Spec} R}^{\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{\mathrm{Spec} R}^n,\quad \alpha_1\otimes\cdots\otimes\alpha_n\mapsto\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge\mathrm{dlog}[\alpha_n].\] We note that $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ would be unchanged if we were to replace Zariski by \'etale in the previous sentence, by \cite[Cor. 4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW}; in particular, $W_1\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ really is the same as $\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ as defined at the start of the subsection. Similarly, if $X$ is a scheme, we let $W_r \Omega_{X, \sub{log}}^n$ denote the sheaf $\mathrm{Spec} R \mapsto W_r \Omega^n_{R, \sub{log}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sheafified de Rham--Witt groups on $\mathbb{F}_p$-schemes and log de Rham--Witt groups as Zariski-local sums of dlog forms.

nodes.name: Geisser--Levine theorem with mod $p^r$ coefficients
nodes.statement: In the case that $R$ is an ind-smooth local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra, Geisser--Levine \cite{GL} established isomorphisms $K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\cong W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ (given by the map $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols) for all $n\ge0$, $r\ge1$, and proved that each group $K_n(R)$ is $p$-torsion-free.
nodes.statement_short: For ind-smooth local $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras, mod $p^r$ K-groups are log de Rham--Witt groups and K-groups are $p$-torsion-free.
conclusions: established isomorphisms $K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\cong W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$
each group $K_n(R)$ is $p$-torsion-free

nodes.name: Pro Geisser--Levine theorem
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, local noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal; fix $n,r\ge 0$. Then the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s $ is $p$-torsion-free and there is a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups \[\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}\}_s\] given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols.
nodes.statement_short: For $F$-finite regular local $R$, pro K-theory of $R/I^s$ is $p$-torsion-free and mod $p^r$ equals pro log de Rham--Witt.
assumptions: $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, local noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal
conclusions: the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s $ is $p$-torsion-free
there is a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups \[\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}\}_s\] given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols
nodes.label: theorem_pro_GL

nodes.name: Relative K-theory mod $p$ of ind-smooth henselian pairs
nodes.statement: Let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras. Suppose that $R$ and $R/I$ are ind-smooth. Then we have a natural isomorphism \begin{equation} K_n(R, I; \mathbb{Z}/p) \simeq \Omega^n_{(R, I), \sub{log}},.\end{equation} where $\Omega^n_{(R, I), \sub{log}}:=\operatorname{ker}(\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}\rightarrow \Omega^n_{R/I,\sub{log}})$.
assumptions: $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
conclusions: we have a natural isomorphism

nodes.name: Relative K-theory mod $p$ as relative log forms
nodes.statement: K_n(R, I; \mathbb{Z}/p) \simeq \Omega^n_{(R, I), \sub{log}},.
nodes.label: relhensmodp

nodes.name: Proof of Relative K-theory mod $p$ of ind-smooth henselian pairs
nodes.statement: Indeed, this follows from our main result (which identifies the relative $K$-theory with relative $\mathrm{TC}$), together with the Geisser--Hesselholt calculations of relative $\mathrm{TC}$. We have the short exact sequence \[ 0 \to \widetilde{\nu}^{n+1}(R) \to \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p) \to \nu^n(R) \to 0 \] as in Theorem~\ref{GHGL} (see also \eqref{thisdiag}). Using Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}, the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem plus Geisser--Hesselholt TC sequence and rigidity of $\widetilde{\nu}$.

nodes.name: Main theorem
nodes.statement: Indeed, this follows from our main result (which identifies the relative $K$-theory with relative $\mathrm{TC}$), together with the Geisser--Hesselholt calculations of relative $\mathrm{TC}$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative K equals relative TC.

nodes.name: Geisser--Hesselholt sequence
nodes.statement: We have the short exact sequence \[ 0 \to \widetilde{\nu}^{n+1}(R) \to \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p) \to \nu^n(R) \to 0 \] as in Theorem~\ref{GHGL} (see also \eqref{thisdiag}).
nodes.statement_short: TC/p in terms of $\nu$.

nodes.name: Rigidity of $\widetilde{\nu}$
nodes.statement: Using Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}, the result follows.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude.

nodes.name: Relative logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: Given an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra $R$ and ideal $I\subseteq R$, we set $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I),\sub{log}}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}\to W_r\Omega^n_{R/I,\sub{log}})$.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of $R-F$ on relative de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$. Then $R-F:W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\to W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)}$ is surjective.
assumptions: $R$ be an $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$
conclusions: $R-F:W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\to W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)}$ is surjective
nodes.label: lemma_drw1

nodes.name: Proof of Surjectivity of $R-F$ on relative de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: If $R$ is $F$-finite, noetherian, and $I$-adically complete then this was proved in \cite[Prop.~2.20]{Morrow-HW}, and we will reduce the general case to this one. Firstly, by taking a filtered colimit we may suppose that $R$ is the henselization of a finite type $\mathbb F_p$-algebra along some ideal, and in particular that $R$ is $F$-finite and excellent \cite[Tag 07QS]{stacks-project}. Then the $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is geometrically regular over $R$ by \cite[7.8.3(v)]{EGA_IV_2}, whence it is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras $A$ by N\'eron--Popescu. But each structure map $R\to A$ admits a splitting as in Remark~\ref{henspairequivtocontinuity}. Therefore, taking a filtered colimit shows that \[\operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)})\] is injective. Since the right side vanishes by the first sentence of the paragraph, the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the $F$-finite complete case via N\'eron--Popescu and split injections.

nodes.name: Known complete case
nodes.statement: If $R$ is $F$-finite, noetherian, and $I$-adically complete then this was proved in \cite[Prop.~2.20]{Morrow-HW}, and we will reduce the general case to this one.
nodes.statement_short: Morrow's result.

nodes.name: Reduce to henselization of finite type
nodes.statement: Firstly, by taking a filtered colimit we may suppose that $R$ is the henselization of a finite type $\mathbb F_p$-algebra along some ideal, and in particular that $R$ is $F$-finite and excellent \cite[Tag 07QS]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: $R$ excellent and $F$-finite.

nodes.name: N\'eron--Popescu
nodes.statement: Then the $I$-adic completion $\widehat R$ is geometrically regular over $R$ by \cite[7.8.3(v)]{EGA_IV_2}, whence it is a filtered colimit of smooth $R$-algebras $A$ by N\'eron--Popescu.
nodes.statement_short: Completion is ind-smooth.

nodes.name: Splittings
nodes.statement: But each structure map $R\to A$ admits a splitting as in Remark~\ref{henspairequivtocontinuity}.
nodes.statement_short: Elkik gives splittings.

nodes.name: Injective cokernel map
nodes.statement: Therefore, taking a filtered colimit shows that \[\operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I)})\longrightarrow \operatorname{Coker}(W_r\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(\widehat R,I\widehat R)})\] is injective.
nodes.statement_short: Cokernel injects into the complete case.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Since the right side vanishes by the first sentence of the paragraph, the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Complete case vanishes.

nodes.name: Illusie's exact sequence for logarithmic de Rham--Witt sheaves
nodes.statement: A important result of Illusie states that if $X$ is a smooth variety over a perfect field of characteristic $p$, then the canonical map of \'etale sheaves $W_{s}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}/p^r\to W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ is an isomorphism whenever $s\ge r$ and $n\ge0$, and therefore \[0\longrightarrow \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r} \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{s-r}\}_s}W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\longrightarrow 0\] is an exact sequence of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$ \cite[\S I.5.7]{illusie-derham-witt}.
assumptions: $X$ is a smooth variety over a perfect field of characteristic $p$
conclusions: the canonical map of \'etale sheaves $W_{s}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}/p^r\to W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ is an isomorphism whenever $s\ge r$ and $n\ge0$

nodes.name: Relative pro exact sequence for logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$; fix $n\ge0$. Then the sequence of pro abelian groups \[0\longrightarrow\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{s-r}\}_s}\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow 0\] is exact for any $r\ge1$.
assumptions: $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$
conclusions: is exact for any $r\ge1$
nodes.label: lemma_drw2

nodes.name: Proof of Relative pro exact sequence for logarithmic de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: We will need to argue via the \'etale topology, so we begin by introducing the necessary sheaves. Let $X:=\mathrm{Spec} R$, with closed subschemes $Y_s:=\mathrm{Spec} R/I^s$ for $s\ge1$; let $W_r\Omega^n_X$, $W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s)}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_X\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s})$ be the corresponding \'etale sheaves on $X$. As explained in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, these sheaves have no higher \'etale cohomology (since $X$ is affine) and their global sections are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_R$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$. Next let $W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ be the image in the \'etale topology of $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\mathbb G_{m,X}^{\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{X}^n$, and similarly for each $Y_s$, and set $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}})$. As we already mentioned in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, the subgroup of dlog forms may be defined using either the Zariski or \'etale topology by \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW}, and therefore the global sections of these sheaves are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}$. We claim that $\{H^1_\sub{\'et}(X,W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}})\}_r=0$ for each $s\ge 1$. After replacing $I$ by $I^s$ (since a subideal of a henselian ideal remains henselian, Remark~\ref{subideal:henspair}) we may as well assume $s=1$ and write $Y=Y_s$ for simplicity of notation; the key will be that $X$ is an affine scheme, henselian along $Y$. Appealing to \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} for both $X$ and $Y$ gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&\{W_r\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}\ar[d]&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{Y,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]&\{W_r\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]&0 }\] Taking the kernels of the vertical arrows gives us a short exact sequence of relative terms \begin{equation}0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0 \end{equation} Since the middle and right terms have no higher cohomology, it is enough to check that $R-F$ is surjective on global sections; but this is even true for each fixed level $r$ by Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}. Finally, appealing to Illusie's result recalled immediately before the lemma (which has been extended to arbitrary regular $\mathbb F_p$-schemes by A.~Shiho \cite[Cor.~2.13]{Shiho2007}) and to an analogous pro version for the formal completion of $X$ along along $Y_1$ \cite[Cor.~4.8]{Morrow-HW} gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are again surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}\ar[d]&\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\ar[d]&W_{r}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}&\{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}&\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]&0 }\] Taking kernels gives a short exact sequence of relative terms \[0\longrightarrow \{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow0.\] Taking global sections completes the proof since the previous paragraph showed that the left term has no $H^1_\sub{\'et}$.
nodes.statement_short: Work with \'etale sheaves; show relative $H^1$ vanishes by surjectivity of $R-F$, then take kernels of Illusie's pro sequences.

nodes.name: \'Etale sheaves
nodes.statement: We will need to argue via the \'etale topology, so we begin by introducing the necessary sheaves. Let $X:=\mathrm{Spec} R$, with closed subschemes $Y_s:=\mathrm{Spec} R/I^s$ for $s\ge1$; let $W_r\Omega^n_X$, $W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s)}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_X\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s})$ be the corresponding \'etale sheaves on $X$. As explained in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, these sheaves have no higher \'etale cohomology (since $X$ is affine) and their global sections are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_R$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative de Rham--Witt sheaves on $X$.

nodes.name: Log sheaves
nodes.statement: Next let $W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}$ be the image in the \'etale topology of $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\mathbb G_{m,X}^{\otimes n}\to W_r\Omega_{X}^n$, and similarly for each $Y_s$, and set $W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}:=\ker(W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\to W_r\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}})$. As we already mentioned in Definition \ref{definition_dRW}, the subgroup of dlog forms may be defined using either the Zariski or \'etale topology by \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW}, and therefore the global sections of these sheaves are respectively $W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$, $W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}$, and $W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative log sheaves.

nodes.name: Vanishing of relative $H^1$
nodes.statement: We claim that $\{H^1_\sub{\'et}(X,W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}})\}_r=0$ for each $s\ge 1$. After replacing $I$ by $I^s$ (since a subideal of a henselian ideal remains henselian, Remark~\ref{subideal:henspair}) we may as well assume $s=1$ and write $Y=Y_s$ for simplicity of notation; the key will be that $X$ is an affine scheme, henselian along $Y$. Appealing to \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} for both $X$ and $Y$ gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&\{W_r\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}\ar[d]&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{Y,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]&\{W_r\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]&0 }\] Taking the kernels of the vertical arrows gives us a short exact sequence of relative terms \begin{equation}0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0 \end{equation} Since the middle and right terms have no higher cohomology, it is enough to check that $R-F$ is surjective on global sections; but this is even true for each fixed level $r$ by Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}.
nodes.statement_short: Relative log $H^1$ vanishes pro-wise.

nodes.name: Reduce to $s=1$
nodes.statement: After replacing $I$ by $I^s$ (since a subideal of a henselian ideal remains henselian, Remark~\ref{subideal:henspair}) we may as well assume $s=1$ and write $Y=Y_s$ for simplicity of notation; the key will be that $X$ is an affine scheme, henselian along $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Subideal remains henselian.

nodes.name: $R-F$ sequences
nodes.statement: Appealing to \cite[Cor.~4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} for both $X$ and $Y$ gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&\{W_r\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}\ar[d]&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_X\}_r\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_r\Omega^n_{Y,\sub{log}}\}_r\ar[r]&\{W_r\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]^{R-F}&\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_Y\}_r\ar[r]&0 }\]
nodes.statement_short: Short exact sequences of pro sheaves.

nodes.name: Relative sequence
nodes.statement: Taking the kernels of the vertical arrows gives us a short exact sequence of relative terms \begin{equation}0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0 \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Relative short exact sequence (24).

nodes.name: Relative $R-F$ short exact sequence of pro sheaves
nodes.statement: 0\longrightarrow \{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y),\sub{log}}\}_r\longrightarrow\{W_r\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\xrightarrow{R-F}\{W_{r-1}\Omega^n_{(X,Y)}\}_r\longrightarrow0
nodes.label: equation_R-F

nodes.name: Surjectivity on global sections
nodes.statement: Since the middle and right terms have no higher cohomology, it is enough to check that $R-F$ is surjective on global sections; but this is even true for each fixed level $r$ by Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma on $R-F$ surjectivity.

nodes.name: Take kernels and global sections
nodes.statement: Finally, appealing to Illusie's result recalled immediately before the lemma (which has been extended to arbitrary regular $\mathbb F_p$-schemes by A.~Shiho \cite[Cor.~2.13]{Shiho2007}) and to an analogous pro version for the formal completion of $X$ along along $Y_1$ \cite[Cor.~4.8]{Morrow-HW} gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are again surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}\ar[d]&\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\ar[d]&W_{r}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}&\{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}&\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]&0 }\] Taking kernels gives a short exact sequence of relative terms \[0\longrightarrow \{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow0.\] Taking global sections completes the proof since the previous paragraph showed that the left term has no $H^1_\sub{\'et}$.
nodes.statement_short: Relative pro sequence and vanishing $H^1$.

nodes.name: Illusie and Shiho
nodes.statement: Finally, appealing to Illusie's result recalled immediately before the lemma (which has been extended to arbitrary regular $\mathbb F_p$-schemes by A.~Shiho \cite[Cor.~2.13]{Shiho2007}) and to an analogous pro version for the formal completion of $X$ along along $Y_1$ \cite[Cor.~4.8]{Morrow-HW} gives rise to short exact sequences of pro sheaves on $X_\sub{\'et}$, in which the three vertical arrows are again surjective: \[\xymatrix{ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}\ar[d]&\{W_s\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\ar[d]&W_{r}\Omega^n_{X,\sub{log}}\ar[r]\ar[d]&0\\ 0\ar[r]& \{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{p^r}&\{W_s\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]^{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}&\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{Y_s,\sub{log}}\}_s\ar[r]&0 }\]
nodes.statement_short: Pro sequences for $X$ and formal completion.

nodes.name: Relative sequence
nodes.statement: Taking kernels gives a short exact sequence of relative terms \[0\longrightarrow \{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{p^r}\{W_s\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\xrightarrow{\{R^{r-s}\}_s}\{W_{r}\Omega^n_{(X,Y_s),\sub{log}}\}_s\longrightarrow0.\]
nodes.statement_short: Kernel sequence.

nodes.name: Global sections
nodes.statement: Taking global sections completes the proof since the previous paragraph showed that the left term has no $H^1_\sub{\'et}$.
nodes.statement_short: Use vanishing $H^1$.

nodes.name: Relative pro Geisser--Levine theorem for henselian ideals
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$; fix $n,r\ge 0$. Then the trace map induces a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups \[\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s.\]
assumptions: $R$ be a $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra which is henselian along an ideal $I\subseteq R$
conclusions: the trace map induces a natural isomorphism of pro abelian groups
nodes.label: theorem_pro_GL_relative

nodes.name: Proof of Relative pro Geisser--Levine theorem for henselian ideals
nodes.statement: The proof is similar to the techniques of \cite[\S5.1]{Morrow-HW}, but we repeat the necessary details here. In particular, we begin with the same recollections on Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg theorems for the spectra $\mathrm{TR}^s$. If $R$ is any $\mathbb F_p$-algebra, then the pro graded ring $\{\mathrm{TR}^s_*(R;p)\}_s$ is a $p$-typical Witt complex with respect to its operators $F,V,R$; by universality of the de Rham--Witt complex, there are therefore natural maps of graded $W_s(R)$-algebras \cite[Prop.~1.5.8]{Hesselholt} $\lambda_{s,R}:W_s\Omega_R^*\to \mathrm{TR}_*^s(R;p)$ for $s\ge0$, which are compatible with the Frobenius, Verschiebung, and Restriction maps (in other words, a morphism of $p$-typical Witt complexes). From now on in the proof assume that $R$ is regular, noetherian, and $F$-finite, and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal. Hesselholt's HKR theorem \cite[Thm.~B]{Hesselholt} implies that the resulting map of pro abelian groups \[\lambda_R:\{W_s\Omega_R^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R;p)\}_s\] is an isomorphism for each $n\ge 1$; similarly, the pro HKR theorem of Dundas--Morrow \cite[Cor.~4.15]{DundasMorrow} implies that \[\lambda_{R/I^\infty}: \{W_s\Omega_{R/I^s}^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s \tag{pro-HKR}\] is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups for each $n\ge0$. Since $W_s\Omega^n_R\to W_s\Omega^n_{R/I^s}$ is surjective for all $s,n\ge0$, it follows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exact sequences and there are therefore natural induced isomorphisms of relative theories \[\{W_s\Omega_{(R,I^s)}^n\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\] for all $n\ge0$. Now assume that $R$ is henselian along $I$. By Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}, the map $R-F:W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$ is surjective for all $n,s\ge0$, and therefore the previous isomorphism shows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\xrightarrow{R-F}\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exacts and thereby induces natural isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;p)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\ker(W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)})\}_s\] The right side of the previous line is precisely $\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by applying \cite[Cor. 4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} to $R$ and $R/I^s$ for each $s\ge1$ (in fact, we have already made this argument: just take global sections in line (\ref{equation_R-F}) for each $Y_s$ and then pass to the resulting diagonal of the $\mathbb N^2$-indexed pro abelian group); moreover, this latter pro abelian group is $p$-torsion-free by the injectivity in Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2} (this is anyway easy: the pro abelian group is contained in $\{W_s\Omega^n_R\}_s$, which is $p$-torsion-free thanks to the equality of the $p$- and canonical-filtrations on the de Rham--Witt groups of any regular $\mathbb F_p$-algebra: see \cite[Prop.~I.3.2 \& I.3.4]{illusie-derham-witt} for the case of a smooth algebra over a perfect field, then apply N\'eron--Popescu), so passing to finite coefficients gives us isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\cong\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}/p^r\}_s\] for each fixed $r\ge1$. The right side is $\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by (the hard part of) Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2}. Finally, pro-constancy of $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(-;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ (Proposition \ref{prop_pro_constant}) implies that the left side of the previous line is $\{\mathrm{TC}_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$, which by Theorem \ref{mainthm} identifies with $\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ via the trace map.
nodes.statement_short: Relative pro HKR and surjectivity of $R-F$ identify relative $\mathrm{TC}^s$ with relative log de Rham--Witt; pro-constancy and the main theorem pass to K-theory.

nodes.name: Witt complex maps
nodes.statement: The proof is similar to the techniques of \cite[\S5.1]{Morrow-HW}, but we repeat the necessary details here. In particular, we begin with the same recollections on Hochschild--Kostant--Rosenberg theorems for the spectra $\mathrm{TR}^s$. If $R$ is any $\mathbb F_p$-algebra, then the pro graded ring $\{\mathrm{TR}^s_*(R;p)\}_s$ is a $p$-typical Witt complex with respect to its operators $F,V,R$; by universality of the de Rham--Witt complex, there are therefore natural maps of graded $W_s(R)$-algebras \cite[Prop.~1.5.8]{Hesselholt} $\lambda_{s,R}:W_s\Omega_R^*\to \mathrm{TR}_*^s(R;p)$ for $s\ge0$, which are compatible with the Frobenius, Verschiebung, and Restriction maps (in other words, a morphism of $p$-typical Witt complexes).
nodes.statement_short: Maps $\lambda_{s,R}$ from de Rham--Witt to TR.

nodes.name: Pro HKR
nodes.statement: From now on in the proof assume that $R$ is regular, noetherian, and $F$-finite, and let $I\subseteq R$ be any ideal. Hesselholt's HKR theorem \cite[Thm.~B]{Hesselholt} implies that the resulting map of pro abelian groups \[\lambda_R:\{W_s\Omega_R^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R;p)\}_s\] is an isomorphism for each $n\ge 1$; similarly, the pro HKR theorem of Dundas--Morrow \cite[Cor.~4.15]{DundasMorrow} implies that \[\lambda_{R/I^\infty}: \{W_s\Omega_{R/I^s}^n\}_s\longrightarrow \{\mathrm{TR}_n^s(R/I^s;p)\}_s \tag{pro-HKR}\] is an isomorphism of pro abelian groups for each $n\ge0$. nodes.statement_short: Relative TR equals relative de Rham--Witt.

nodes.name: Relative $\mathrm{TC}^s$
nodes.statement: Now assume that $R$ is henselian along $I$. By Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}, the map $R-F:W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$ is surjective for all $n,s\ge0$, and therefore the previous isomorphism shows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\xrightarrow{R-F}\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exacts and thereby induces natural isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;p)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\ker(W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)})\}_s\] The right side of the previous line is precisely $\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by applying \cite[Cor. 4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} to $R$ and $R/I^s$ for each $s\ge1$ (in fact, we have already made this argument: just take global sections in line (\ref{equation_R-F}) for each $Y_s$ and then pass to the resulting diagonal of the $\mathbb N^2$-indexed pro abelian group); moreover, this latter pro abelian group is $p$-torsion-free by the injectivity in Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2} (this is anyway easy: the pro abelian group is contained in $\{W_s\Omega^n_R\}_s$, which is $p$-torsion-free thanks to the equality of the $p$- and canonical-filtrations on the de Rham--Witt groups of any regular $\mathbb F_p$-algebra: see \cite[Prop.~I.3.2 \& I.3.4]{illusie-derham-witt} for the case of a smooth algebra over a perfect field, then apply N\'eron--Popescu), so passing to finite coefficients gives us isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\cong\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}/p^r\}_s\] for each fixed $r\ge1$. The right side is $\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by (the hard part of) Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2}.
nodes.statement_short: Identify relative $\mathrm{TC}^s$ with relative log forms mod $p^r$.

nodes.name: $R-F$ surjective
nodes.statement: Now assume that $R$ is henselian along $I$. By Lemma \ref{lemma_drw1}, the map $R-F:W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\to W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}$ is surjective for all $n,s\ge0$, and therefore the previous isomorphism shows that the long exact sequence associated to $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\to \{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s\xrightarrow{R-F}\{\mathrm{TR}^s(R,I^s;p)\}_s$ breaks into short exacts and thereby induces natural isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;p)\}_s\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} \{\ker(W_{s}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)}\xrightarrow{R-F} W_{s-1}\Omega^n_{(R,I^s)})\}_s\]
nodes.statement_short: Long exact sequence splits.

nodes.name: Log forms and torsion-freeness
nodes.statement: The right side of the previous line is precisely $\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by applying \cite[Cor. 4.1(iii)]{Morrow-HW} to $R$ and $R/I^s$ for each $s\ge1$ (in fact, we have already made this argument: just take global sections in line (\ref{equation_R-F}) for each $Y_s$ and then pass to the resulting diagonal of the $\mathbb N^2$-indexed pro abelian group); moreover, this latter pro abelian group is $p$-torsion-free by the injectivity in Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2} (this is anyway easy: the pro abelian group is contained in $\{W_s\Omega^n_R\}_s$, which is $p$-torsion-free thanks to the equality of the $p$- and canonical-filtrations on the de Rham--Witt groups of any regular $\mathbb F_p$-algebra: see \cite[Prop.~I.3.2 \& I.3.4]{illusie-derham-witt} for the case of a smooth algebra over a perfect field, then apply N\'eron--Popescu), so passing to finite coefficients gives us isomorphisms \[\{\mathrm{TC}^s_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\cong\{W_s\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}/p^r\}_s\] for each fixed $r\ge1$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify with log forms; $p$-torsion-free.

nodes.name: Mod $p^r$
nodes.statement: The right side is $\{W_r\Omega^n_{(R,I^s),\sub{log}}\}_s$ by (the hard part of) Lemma \ref{lemma_drw2}.
nodes.statement_short: Relative pro exact sequence lemma.

nodes.name: Pass to K-theory
nodes.statement: Finally, pro-constancy of $\{\mathrm{TC}^s(-;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ (Proposition \ref{prop_pro_constant}) implies that the left side of the previous line is $\{\mathrm{TC}_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$, which by Theorem \ref{mainthm} identifies with $\{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ via the trace map.
nodes.statement_short: Pro-constancy and the main theorem.

nodes.name: The pro Geisser--Levine theorem holds
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL} is true.

nodes.name: Proof of The pro Geisser--Levine theorem holds
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be as in the statement of Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL}. Without loss of generality $R$ is henselian along $I$, whence $R$ is also local, and so the result follows by combining Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL_relative} with the isomorphism $K_n(R; \mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ of Geisser--Levine \cite{GL}. Note that the two results are compatible since the trace map is given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols by \cite[Lem.~4.2.3 \& Cor.~6.4.1]{GH}. We establish the $p$-torsion-freeness of $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ in the next corollary.
nodes.statement_short: Combine relative pro Geisser--Levine with absolute Geisser--Levine.

nodes.name: Combine relative and absolute
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be as in the statement of Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL}. Without loss of generality $R$ is henselian along $I$, whence $R$ is also local, and so the result follows by combining Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL_relative} with the isomorphism $K_n(R; \mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\stackrel{\simeq}{\to} W_r\Omega^n_{R,\sub{log}}$ of Geisser--Levine \cite{GL}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to henselian and combine.

nodes.name: Compatibility
nodes.statement: Note that the two results are compatible since the trace map is given by $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]$ on symbols by \cite[Lem.~4.2.3 \& Cor.~6.4.1]{GH}.
nodes.statement_short: Trace is dlog on symbols.

nodes.name: Pointer

nodes.name: Comparison to Milnor K-theory; $p$-torsion-freeness
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that $R/I$ is local. Then, for all $n,r\ge0$: \begin{enumerate} \item the canonical map $\{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\to\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ is surjective and has the same kernel as $\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]:\{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\to \{W_r\Omega^n_{R/I^s}\}_s$; \item the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ is $p$-torsion-free. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that $R/I$ is local
conclusions: the canonical map $\{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\to\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r)\}_s$ is surjective
the pro abelian group $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s$ is $p$-torsion-free
nodes.label: corollary_Milnor

nodes.name: Proof of Comparison to Milnor K-theory; $p$-torsion-freeness
nodes.statement: We can replace $R$ by its $I$-adic completion and thereby assume $R$ itself is local. Part (1) is an immediate consequence of the commutative diagram \[\xymatrix{ \{K_n^M(R/I^s)/p^r\}_s\ar[r]\ar@/_1cm/[rr]_{\mathrm{dlog}[\cdot]}& \{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\ar[r]^{\cong}&\{W_r\Omega_{R/I^s,\sub{log}}^n\}_s }\] which summarises the statement of Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL}, since the bendy arrow is surjective. Part (1) clearly implies that $\{K_n(R/I^s)\}_s\to \{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is surjective, whence the usual exact sequence implies it is an isomorphism and that $\{K_{n-1}(R/I^s)[p]\}_s=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Diagram chase from the pro Geisser--Levine theorem.

nodes.name: Lifting classes
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian, local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal. Then, for all $n,r\ge0$: \begin{enumerate} \item the sequences \[0\longrightarrow \{K_n(R,I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\longrightarrow K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s\longrightarrow 0\] are short exact; \item there exists $s\ge 1$ with the following property: if an element of $K_n(R/I;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)$ lifts to $K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)$, then it is symbolic and hence lifts to $K_n(R)$. \end{enumerate}
assumptions: $R$ be an $F$-finite, regular, noetherian, local $\mathbb F_p$-algebra and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal
conclusions: are short exact
there exists $s\ge 1$ with the following property
nodes.label: corollary_lifting

nodes.name: Proof of Lifting classes
nodes.statement: As we have just seen in Corollary \ref{corollary_Milnor}, $\{K_n(R/I^s;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is entirely symbolic; since $R\to R/I$ is surjective on units (using the assumption $I\subseteq\operatorname{Jac}(R)$), we deduce that $K_n(R;\mathbb Z/p^r\mathbb Z)\to \{K_n(R/I^s;p^r\mathbb Z/\mathbb Z)\}_s$ is surjective for all $n\ge0$. Therefore the long exact relative sequences breaks into the desired short exact sequences. Part (2) is a consequence of the surjectivity arguments of the previous paragraph, unravelling what it means for a map of pro abelian groups to be surjective.
nodes.statement_short: Pro groups are symbolic and units surject, so the long exact sequence splits.

nodes.name: Relative pro Geisser--Levine

nodes.statement: This follows from the short exact sequence of Corollary \ref{corollary_lifting}(1) by applying usual Geisser--Levine to the middle term and Theorem \ref{theorem_pro_GL} to the right term.

nodes.name: Strictly henselian local ring
nodes.statement: Recall that a local ring is called \emph{strictly henselian} if it is henselian local and its residue field is separably closed.
differentia: it is henselian local and its residue field is separably closed

nodes.name: \'Etale K-theory is TC at points of characteristic $p$
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring of residue characteristic $p$. Then $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)/p =0$, i.e., the map $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence.
assumptions: $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring of residue characteristic $p$
conclusions: $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)/p =0$
the map $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence
also_stated_at: Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local ring with residue field of characteristic $p > 0$. Then $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(R)/p = 0$, i.e., the map $K(R) \to \mathrm{TC}(R)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence.
nodes.label: etalekthm

nodes.name: Proof of \'Etale K-theory is TC at points of characteristic $p$
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we may assume that $R=k$ is a field itself, which is then separably closed. Thus we need to show that if $k$ is a separably closed field of characteristic $p > 0$, then the map $K(k) \to \mathrm{TC}(k)$ is a $p$-adic equivalence. As $\mathbb{F}_p$ is perfect, $k$ is an ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra (e.g., choose a transcendence basis for $k$). Thus it suffices to show that the terms $\widetilde{\nu}^n(k)$ vanish by Theorem~\ref{GHGL}. That is, we need to show that the map \[ 1 - C^{-1}: \Omega^n_k \to \Omega^n_k/ d \Omega^{n-1}_k \] is surjective. Given a form $\omega = a dx_1 \dots dx_n \in \Omega^n_k$, we have $(1 - C^{-1})(u \omega) = (u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1}) \omega$. Since $k$ is separably closed, we can solve the equation $ u - u^p a^{p-1} x_1^{p-1} \dots x_n^{p-1} = 1$ in $k$. This implies that $1 - C^{-1}$ is surjective as desired and completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to separably closed fields by rigidity; show $1-C^{-1}$ is surjective by solving an Artin--Schreier type equation.

nodes.name: Alternative argument for \'etale K-theory via Suslin
nodes.statement: In the proof above, rather than using Theorem \ref{GHGL} and the groups $\widetilde{\nu}^n(k)$, one can instead follow Suslin's arguments from \cite{Suslinalgclosed} to show invariance of $K^{\mathrm{inv}}(-)/p$ under extensions of separably closed fields. This reduces to the case $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}_p}$, which is easy since $K/p$ and $\mathrm{TC}/p$ can be directly calculated, cf.~\cite{HM97, Qui} or Example \ref{perfex}.
nodes.statement_short: Use Suslin's invariance under separably closed field extensions to reduce to $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$, computed directly.

nodes.name: Suslin's invariance under extensions of separably closed fields
nodes.statement: Let $F: \mathrm{Ring} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ be a functor from rings to abelian groups. Suppose that $F$ commutes with filtered colimits and satisfies rigidity, i.e., for a henselian pair $(R, I)$ we have $F(R) \simeq F(R/I)$. Then for an extension $K \to L$ of separably closed fields, we have $F(K) \simeq F(L)$.
assumptions: $F: \mathrm{Ring} \to \mathrm{Ab}$ be a functor from rings to abelian groups
$F$ commutes with filtered colimits and satisfies rigidity
conclusions: for an extension $K \to L$ of separably closed fields, we have $F(K) \simeq F(L)$

nodes.name: Proof of Suslin's invariance under extensions of separably closed fields
nodes.statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field. The crux of Suslin's argument is to show that if $q:X\rightarrow\mathrm{Spec}(k)$ is a connected smooth affine $k$-scheme of finite type, then for any class $\alpha \in F(X)$ and section $x: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$, the pullback $x^* \alpha \in F(k)$ is independent of the choice of $x$. It suffices to fix a section $x_0: \mathrm{Spec}(k) \to X$, and show (by connectedness, in view of the Zariski density of $k$-points in $X$, cf., e.g., \cite[Tag 04QM]{stacks-project}) that there exists a Zariski neighborhood $U$ of $x_0$ such that $x_0^\ast\alpha = x^\ast\alpha$ for all sections $x:\mathrm{Spec}(k)\rightarrow U$. Replacing $\alpha$ by $\alpha-q^\ast x_0^\ast \alpha$, we can assume $x^\ast\alpha=0$. Then by the assumption of rigidity, applied to the henselization of $X$ at $x_0$, and the commutation of $F$ with filtered colimits, we deduce that there is an \'etale neighborhood $Y\rightarrow X$ of $x_0$ such that $\alpha$ pulls back to $0$ on $Y$. Then we can take $U$ to be the image of $Y\rightarrow X$: as $k$ is separably closed, every $k$-point of $U$ lifts to $Y$. Now we prove the proposition. It suffices to consider the case where $K$ is the separable closure of a prime field, and so is in particular perfect. Therefore, the extension $K \to L$ is ind-smooth, i.e., $L$ is a filtered colimit of smooth $K$-algebras $A_\alpha$, with $\alpha$ running over a filtered poset. Then each map $K \to A_\alpha$ admits a retraction, as $K$ is separably closed. It follows that $F(K) \to F(A_\alpha)$ is injective for each $\alpha$, so that $F(K) \to F(L)$ is injective. We now argue surjectivity. Let $u \in F(A_\alpha)$; we show that the image of $u$ in $F(L)$ belongs to the image of $F(K)$. Passing to a component if necessary, we can assume $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha)$ is connected. Then $\mathrm{Spec}(A_\alpha\otimes_K L)$ is connected as well, since $K$ is algebraically closed. Now consider the two maps \[ f_1, f_2:A_\alpha \rightrightarrows L, \] where the first map is the colimit structure map and where where the second map is $A_\alpha \stackrel{s}{\to} K \to L$. By the first paragraph of the argument applied to the $L$-algebra $A_\alpha \otimes_K L$, we conclude that these two maps have the same effect on $u$, verifying the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Suslin's argument: pullbacks along sections of smooth connected varieties agree by rigidity at henselizations; retractions give injectivity and surjectivity.

nodes.name: \'Etale homotopy sheaves $\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)$ and $\pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)$
nodes.statement: Let $\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)$ denote the \'etale sheafification of the functor $\pi_n (K(-)/p)$ over an arbitrary scheme $X$, and let $\pi_n( \mathcal{TC}/p)$ denote the same for $\pi_n (\mathrm{TC}(-)/p)$.

nodes.name: Sheaf-theoretic reformulation of the \'etale comparison
nodes.statement: Then if $i$ denotes the closed inclusion $(X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{Z})}\mathrm{Spec}(\mathbb{F}_p))_{et}\rightarrow X_{et}$, Theorem \ref{etalekthm} (plus the trivial fact that $\mathrm{TC} /p$ vanishes on rings where $p$ is invertible) is equivalent to the statement that for all $n$, there is an equivalence \begin{equation} \pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)\simeq i_\ast i^\ast \pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)\end{equation} adjoint to the map $i^\ast\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)\rightarrow i^\ast \pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)$ (also an equivalence) given by the restriction of the cyclotomic trace.
conclusions: for all $n$, there is an equivalence

nodes.name: TC/p sheaves as pushforward of K/p sheaves
nodes.statement: \pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)\simeq i_\ast i^\ast \pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)

nodes.name: $p$-adic \'etale K-theory is TC for proper schemes
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme proper over $\mathrm{Spec} R$ for a ring $R$ henselian along $(p)$. Denote by $\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(-)$ the \'etale Postnikov sheafification of the $K$-theory presheaf, meaning the limit over the \'etale sheafified Postnikov tower of $K(-)$.\footnote{This is what Thomason's \'etale hypercohomology construction implements. By \cite[Thm.~1.3]{CM18} it agrees with the more basic sheafification for the etale site as considered in \cite{HTT} under very mild finiteness assumptions on $X$. We refer also to \cite[Sec.~1.3]{SAG} as a source for sheaves of spectra and the associated $t$-structure.} Then the natural map $$\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(X)/p\rightarrow \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$$ is an equivalence.
assumptions: $X$ be a scheme proper over $\mathrm{Spec} R$ for a ring $R$ henselian along $(p)$
conclusions: the natural map $$\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(X)/p\rightarrow \mathrm{TC}(X)/p$$ is an equivalence
nodes.label: padicetaleKthy

nodes.name: Proof of $p$-adic \'etale K-theory is TC for proper schemes
nodes.statement: The comparison map is induced by the cyclotomic trace, given that $\mathrm{TC}/p$ is an \'etale Postnikov sheaf (see \cite[Thm 5.16]{CM18} in full generality; for affines, see \cite[Sec.~3]{GH}; in the semi-separated case see \cite{BMloc} for the conclusion of Nisnevich descent). Now assume $X$ is proper over $\mathrm{Spec}(R)$ henselian along $(p)$. Then the proper base change theorem together with Gabber's affine analog of the proper base change theorem \cite{Gabberaffine} combine to show $H^j_\sub{\'et}(X, \mathcal{F})\simeq H^j_\sub{\'et}(X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(R)}\mathrm{Spec}(R/pR), i^*\mathcal{F})$ for all torsion abelian sheaves $\mathcal{F}$ on $X_{et}$. In particular, $X_{et}$ has finite $p$-cohomological dimension by induction on an affine cover and the following Lemma~\ref{finiteetale}, so by comparing descent spectral sequences for $\widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(X)$ and $\mathrm{TC}(X)$ it suffices to show that $\pi_n(\mathcal{K}/p)$ and $\pi_n(\mathcal{TC}/p)$ have the same cohomology on $X_\sub{\'et}$. But by the same base change results, this follows from the fact (see above) that they have the same restriction to $X\times_{\mathrm{Spec}(R)}\mathrm{Spec}(R/pR)$.
nodes.statement_short: Proper base change reduces to the special fiber, where \'etale sheaves of K/p and TC/p agree.
