nodes.name: Proof of Mod $p$ \'etale cohomological dimension of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
nodes.statement: This is classical in the noetherian case from the Artin-Schreier sequence (see \cite[Exp.~X, Thm.~5.1]{SGA4}). To obtain the non-noetherian case, we use the criterion from \cite[Exp. IX, Prop.~5.5]{SGA4} together with the fact that cohomology commutes with filtered colimits \cite[Tag 03Q4]{stacks-project}.
nodes.statement_short: Artin--Schreier sequence in the noetherian case; pass to filtered colimits.

nodes.name: Asymptotic comparison of K and TC
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $p$ be a prime number. Suppose that $d \geq 1$ and: \begin{enumerate} \item $R$ is henselian along $(p)$. \item The ring $R/p$ has finite Krull dimension. \item For any $x \in \mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$, the residue field $k(x)$ has the property that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$. \end{enumerate} The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for any $r$.
nodes.statement_short: For $R$ henselian along $p$ with finite-dimensional $R/p$ and bounded $p$-degrees of residue fields, $K/p^r\to\mathrm{TC}/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$.
assumptions: $R$ be a commutative ring and $p$ be a prime number
The ring $R/p$ has finite Krull dimension.
For any $x \in \mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$, the residue field $k(x)$ has the property that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$.
conclusions: The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for any $r$
also_stated_at: \label{KTCinlarge} Let $R$ be a ring henselian along $(p)$ and such that $R/p$ has finite Krull dimension. Let $d = \sup_{x \in \mathrm{Spec} (R/p) } \log_p [k(x): k(x)^p]$ where $k(x)$ denotes the residue field at $x$ and $k(x)^p \subset k(x)$ the subfield of $p^\sub{th}$ powers. Then the map $K(R)/p^i \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^i$ is a equivalence in degrees $\geq \max(d, 1)$ for each $i \geq 1$.
nodes.label: KTCasymptotic

nodes.name: Proof of Asymptotic comparison of K and TC
nodes.statement: We use throughout the following basic observation: if $T \to T'$ is a map of spectra which is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$, then for any spectrum $T''$ with a map $T'' \to T'$, the map $T \times_{T'} T'' \to T''$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$. Using the pullback square from Theorem~\ref{mainthm} (involving the spectra $K(R)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r, K(R/p)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R/p)/p^r$), we reduce to the case where $R$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. It now suffices to see that $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$. Note also that the result is clearly equivalent if we replace $K(R)/p$ with $\mathbb{K}(R)/p$. By the theorems of Thomason--Trobaugh \cite{TT90} and Blumberg--Mandell \cite{BMloc} respectively, $\mathbb{K}(-)/p^r$ and $\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r$ are Nisnevich sheaves on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ with values in the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sp}$. By \cite[Th.~3.17]{CM18}, the finiteness of Krull dimension implies that the Nisnevich topos of $\mathrm{Spec} R$ has \emph{finite homotopy dimension} in the sense of \cite[Def. 7.2.2.1]{HTT}. In the case where $R$ is noetherian, the finiteness of homotopy dimension appears in \cite[Thm.~3.7.7.1]{SAG}. As a consequence, Postnikov towers in the $\infty$-category of Nisnevich sheaves of spectra on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ are convergent and one has a descent spectral sequence. Therefore, it suffices to see that the maps on stalks induce isomorphisms in degrees $\geq d$. The maps on stalks are \[ \mathbb{K}(A)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p^r, \] as $A$ ranges over the connected finite \'etale algebras over henselizations of $R$ at prime ideals. Since the map $K(A)/p \to \mathbb{K}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 1$, it suffices to see that $K(A)/p \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for each such $A$. This in turn follows from the fiber square of Theorem~\ref{mainthm} (applied to the henselian local ring $A$) and the fact that if $k$ is a field of characteristic $p$, then the map $K(k)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(k)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq \log_p [k: k^p]$ (which follows from Theorem~\ref{GHGL} and the theory of $p$-bases, which implies $\dim \Omega^1_k \leq d$ and so $\Omega^n_k = 0$ for $n > d$ \cite[Thm.~26.5]{Matsumura}). Note also that the invariant $\log_p [k:k^p] = \dim \Omega^1_k$ is invariant under finite separable extensions of fields of characteristic $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras by the main theorem, then to stalks by Nisnevich descent with finite homotopy dimension; use $p$-bases for fields.

nodes.name: Pullback observation
nodes.statement: We use throughout the following basic observation: if $T \to T'$ is a map of spectra which is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$, then for any spectrum $T''$ with a map $T'' \to T'$, the map $T \times_{T'} T'' \to T''$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$.
nodes.statement_short: Equivalences in a range pull back.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
nodes.statement: Using the pullback square from Theorem~\ref{mainthm} (involving the spectra $K(R)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r, K(R/p)/p^r, \mathrm{TC}(R/p)/p^r$), we reduce to the case where $R$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. It now suffices to see that $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem.

nodes.name: Nisnevich sheaves
nodes.statement: Note also that the result is clearly equivalent if we replace $K(R)/p$ with $\mathbb{K}(R)/p$. By the theorems of Thomason--Trobaugh \cite{TT90} and Blumberg--Mandell \cite{BMloc} respectively, $\mathbb{K}(-)/p^r$ and $\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r$ are Nisnevich sheaves on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ with values in the $\infty$-category $\mathrm{Sp}$.
nodes.statement_short: Thomason--Trobaugh and Blumberg--Mandell.

nodes.name: Finite homotopy dimension
nodes.statement: By \cite[Th.~3.17]{CM18}, the finiteness of Krull dimension implies that the Nisnevich topos of $\mathrm{Spec} R$ has \emph{finite homotopy dimension} in the sense of \cite[Def. 7.2.2.1]{HTT}. In the case where $R$ is noetherian, the finiteness of homotopy dimension appears in \cite[Thm.~3.7.7.1]{SAG}. As a consequence, Postnikov towers in the $\infty$-category of Nisnevich sheaves of spectra on $\mathrm{Spec} R$ are convergent and one has a descent spectral sequence.
nodes.statement_short: Descent spectral sequence converges.

nodes.name: Reduce to stalks
nodes.statement: Therefore, it suffices to see that the maps on stalks induce isomorphisms in degrees $\geq d$. The maps on stalks are \[ \mathbb{K}(A)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p^r, \] as $A$ ranges over the connected finite \'etale algebras over henselizations of $R$ at prime ideals.
nodes.statement_short: Henselian local stalks.

nodes.name: Connective version
nodes.statement: Since the map $K(A)/p \to \mathbb{K}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 1$, it suffices to see that $K(A)/p \to \mathrm{TC}(A)/p$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ for each such $A$.
nodes.statement_short: Replace $\mathbb{K}$ by $K$.

nodes.name: Fields
nodes.statement: This in turn follows from the fiber square of Theorem~\ref{mainthm} (applied to the henselian local ring $A$) and the fact that if $k$ is a field of characteristic $p$, then the map $K(k)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(k)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq \log_p [k: k^p]$ (which follows from Theorem~\ref{GHGL} and the theory of $p$-bases, which implies $\dim \Omega^1_k \leq d$ and so $\Omega^n_k = 0$ for $n > d$ \cite[Thm.~26.5]{Matsumura}). Note also that the invariant $\log_p [k:k^p] = \dim \Omega^1_k$ is invariant under finite separable extensions of fields of characteristic $p$.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem and $p$-bases for fields.

nodes.name: $p$-adic Lichtenbaum--Quillen comparison
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$ with $\mathrm{Spec}(R/p)$ of finite Krull dimension, and suppose that $d\ge1$ is such that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$ for all $x\in\mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$. Then the map $K(R)/p^r\to \widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\ge d$ for any $r$.
assumptions: $R$ be a commutative ring which is henselian along $(p)$ with $\mathrm{Spec}(R/p)$ of finite Krull dimension
$d\ge1$ is such that $[k(x): k(x)^p] \leq p^d$ for all $x\in\mathrm{Spec} (R/p)$
conclusions: the map $K(R)/p^r\to \widehat{K}^\sub{\'et}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\ge d$ for any $r$

nodes.name: Proof of $p$-adic Lichtenbaum--Quillen comparison
nodes.statement: Combine Theorems \ref{KTCasymptotic} and \ref{padicetaleKthy}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the asymptotic comparison with the \'etale comparison.

nodes.name: $F$-finite noetherian $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a noetherian $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra which is \emph{$F$-finite,} i.e., the Frobenius map is finite (Definition~\ref{Ffinite}). Then $R$ has finite Krull dimension \cite[Prop. 1.1]{Kunz}. Moreover, if $R$ is generated as a module by $p^d$ elements over the Frobenius, this passes to any localization. It follows that if $k$ is any residue field of $R$, then $[k: k^p] \leq p^d$. Therefore, the map $K(R)/p \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p $ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq d$ thanks to Theorem~\ref{KTCasymptotic}. Note that Theorem~\ref{KTCasymptotic} assumes that $d \geq 1$, but if $d = 0$ then $R$ is a finite product of perfect fields, so that the result follows from Example~\ref{perfex} below.

nodes.name: Perfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra, i.e., such that the Frobenius is an isomorphism. Then the map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence on connective covers for each $r \geq 0$. In fact, $\mathrm{TC}_i(R)$ vanishes for $i > 0$. This follows as in the calculation of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathbb{F}_p)$ in \cite[Sec.~IV-4]{nikolaus-scholze}. Indeed, by a variant of B\"okstedt's calculation, one finds $\mathrm{THH}(R)_* \simeq R[\sigma]$ for $|\sigma| = 2$ and $$ \mathrm{TC}^-_*(R) = W(R)[x, \sigma]/(x \sigma - p), \quad \mathrm{TP}_*(R) \simeq W(R)[x^{\pm 1}], \quad |x| = -2.$$ If $R$ has no nontrivial idempotents, it follows that $\pi_0(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r) = \mathbb{Z}/p^r \mathbb{Z}$ and that $\pi_{-1}(\mathrm{TC}_{}(R)/p^r)$ is the cokernel of $F -1 $ on $W_r(R)$. We refer to the work of Bhatt--Morrow--Scholze \cite{BMS2} for more details. Moreover, $K_i(R)$ is a $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$-module for $i > 0$. This follows from the existence of Adams operations in higher $K$-theory and the fact that $\psi^p$ is the Frobenius, cf.~\cite{Hiller, Kratzer}. If $R$ has no nontrivial idempotents, it follows by Zariski descent that the kernel of the map $K_0(R) \to \mathbb{Z}$ is a $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$-module, so that $K_0(R)/p \simeq \mathbb{Z}/p$. Combining all these observations, the claim for $R$ follows provided $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is connected. To reduce the general case to that one, note that everything commutes with filtered colimits, so we can assume $R$ is the perfection of a finite type $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is noetherian, hence a finite disjoint union of connected affines, giving the reduction.
nodes.statement_short: For perfect $R$, $K/p^r\to\mathrm{TC}/p^r$ is an equivalence on connective covers, as positive TC vanishes and positive K is $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$-linear.
nodes.label: perfex

nodes.name: K and TC of rings with semiperfect reduction
nodes.statement: Let $R$ be a ring henselian along $(p)$. Suppose $R/p$ is a \emph{semiperfect} ring, i.e., an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra such that the Frobenius map on $R/p$ is a surjection. The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$ for any $r$.
conclusions: The map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$ for any $r$
nodes.label: Kpfd

nodes.name: Proof of K and TC of rings with semiperfect reduction
nodes.statement: Using Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we immediately reduce to the case where $R$ itself is a semiperfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra. In this case, let $I \subset R$ be the nilradical. It follows that $R/I$ is perfect and that $I$ is locally nilpotent, so that $(R, I)$ is a henselian pair. By Theorem~\ref{mainthm} and Example~\ref{perfex}, it follows that the map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to semiperfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras and then to perfect ones by the main theorem.

nodes.name: Reduce to $\mathbb{F}_p$
nodes.statement: Using Theorem~\ref{mainthm}, we immediately reduce to the case where $R$ itself is a semiperfect $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra.
nodes.statement_short: Main theorem.

nodes.name: Nilradical
nodes.statement: In this case, let $I \subset R$ be the nilradical. It follows that $R/I$ is perfect and that $I$ is locally nilpotent, so that $(R, I)$ is a henselian pair.
nodes.statement_short: $(R,I)$ is henselian with perfect quotient.

nodes.name: Perfect case
nodes.statement: By Theorem~\ref{mainthm} and Example~\ref{perfex}, it follows that the map $K(R)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r$ is an equivalence in degrees $\geq 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Perfect example.

nodes.name: Rings of integers in complete nonarchimedean fields
nodes.statement: Let $C$ be a complete nonarchimedean field whose residue field is perfect of characteristic $p$. Let $\mathcal{O}_C \subset C$ be the ring of integers, and let $\pi \in \mathcal{O}_C$ be a nonzero element of positive valuation. Then $\mathcal{O}_C$ is $\pi$-adically complete, and the image of the maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}_C \subset \mathcal{O}_C$ is a locally nilpotent ideal in $\mathcal{O}_C/\pi$: in particular, $\mathfrak{m}_C \subset \mathcal{O}_C$ is henselian. We conclude that the map $K( \mathcal{O}_C)/p^r \to \mathrm{TC}( \mathcal{O}_C)/p^r$ exhibits the former as the connective cover of the latter for $r \geq 0$ since we know the analogous statement for the residue field (as in Example~\ref{perfex}). Given a perfectoid field $C$ (in the sense of \cite{Scholze}), the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_C$ has perfect residue field, so the above conclusion holds. When $C = \mathbb{C}_p$ is the completed algebraic closure of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, the $p$-adic $K$-theory of $\mathcal{O}_C$ was calculated by Nizio\l, cf.~\cite[Lem~3.1]{Niziol-crystalline} which shows that $K(\mathcal{O}_C; \mathbb{Z}_p) \simeq K(C; \mathbb{C}_p)$, which in turn is $p$-adic connective topological $K$-theory by \cite{Suslinalgclosed, Suslinlocal}. Similarly, $\mathrm{TC}(\mathcal{O}_C; \mathbb{Z}_p)$ was calculated by Hesselholt \cite{HesselholtOC} and shown to agree with the $K$-theory. A description of $\mathrm{TC}(\mathcal{O}_C; \mathbb{Z}_p)$ in general has been given in \cite{BMS2}.

nodes.name: Split injectivity of the cyclotomic trace
nodes.statement_short: For local $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras the trace on mod $p^r$ homotopy is split injective, with functorial complement $\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}$.
conclusions: the trace map $\pi_n (K(R)/p^r) \to \pi_n (\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r)$ is split injective
$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}$ commutes with filtered colimits
also_stated_at: For any local $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$ and any $i \geq 1$, the cyclotomic trace $K(R)/p^i \to \mathrm{TC}(R)/p^i$ is split injective on homotopy groups.
nodes.label: injectivityresult

nodes.name: Proof of Split injectivity of the cyclotomic trace
nodes.statement_short: Construct a functorial ind-smooth henselian cover $R'\to R$ and define the complement via \'etale $H^1$; split by Geisser--Levine/Hesselholt and the main theorem.

nodes.name: Functorial cover $R'$
nodes.statement: Recall that if $R$ is an $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra, we can make a functorial surjection to $R$ from a polynomial algebra, namely take the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{F}_p[x_a]_{a\in R}$ on variables indexed by the elements of $R$ with the map $x_a\mapsto a$. Let $R'\rightarrow R$ denote the henselization of this surjection at its kernel; thus $R'$ is a functorial ind-smooth $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra surjecting onto $R$ with henselian kernel. Moreover, $R\mapsto R'$ evidently commutes with filtered colimits.
nodes.statement_short: Henselized polynomial cover.

nodes.name: Define $\widetilde{\nu^m_r}$
nodes.statement: Define for $m \geq 0$ $$\widetilde{\nu^m_r}(R) := H^1(\operatorname{Spec}(R')_\sub{\'{e}t};\pi_{m}(\mathcal{TC}/p^r)).$$ Since the coefficient presheaf $\pi_{m}(\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r)$ commutes with filtered colimits by Corollary \ref{TCring}, this \'etale cohomology group commutes with filtered colimits in $R'$ by standard cocontinuity arguments. Combining with the previous, we find that $\widetilde{\nu^m_r}(-)$ commutes with filtered colimits.
nodes.statement_short: \'Etale $H^1$ of TC sheaves; commutes with filtered colimits.

nodes.name: Natural transformation
nodes.statement: Furthermore, since $\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ has \'{e}tale $p$-cohomological dimension $\leq 1$, the descent spectral sequence for $\mathrm{TC}(-)/p^r$ gives a natural map $\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r)$ (compare with the proofs of Theorem \ref{GHGL} and Theorem \ref{padicetaleKthy}). Composing with the map on $\mathrm{TC}$ induced by $R'\rightarrow R$ defines the desired natural transformation $\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r)$.
nodes.statement_short: Descent spectral sequence.

nodes.name: Local case
nodes.statement: Now assume $R$ is local. Then $R'$ is too, since a henselian ideal is radical, and it is moreover ind-smooth. Thus the argument recalled before the statement of the theorem, based on the results of Geisser--Levine and Geisser--Hesselholt, shows that $$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\oplus \pi_n(K(R')/p^r)\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r).$$ On the other hand our main rigidity theorem, Theorem \ref{mainthm}, gives a long exact sequence $$\ldots\rightarrow\pi_n(K(R')/p^r)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r)\oplus \pi_n(K(R)/p^r)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r)\rightarrow\ldots.$$ Combining shows both that this long exact sequence breaks up into short exact sequences and that $$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\oplus\pi_n(K(R)/p^r)\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r),$$ as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Split via ind-smooth case and main theorem.

nodes.name: $R'$ local ind-smooth
nodes.statement: Now assume $R$ is local. Then $R'$ is too, since a henselian ideal is radical, and it is moreover ind-smooth.
nodes.statement_short: Henselian ideals are radical.

nodes.name: Ind-smooth splitting
nodes.statement: Thus the argument recalled before the statement of the theorem, based on the results of Geisser--Levine and Geisser--Hesselholt, shows that $$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\oplus \pi_n(K(R')/p^r)\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r).$$
nodes.statement_short: Geisser--Levine/Hesselholt.

nodes.name: Main theorem
nodes.statement: On the other hand our main rigidity theorem, Theorem \ref{mainthm}, gives a long exact sequence $$\ldots\rightarrow\pi_n(K(R')/p^r)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R')/p^r)\oplus \pi_n(K(R)/p^r)\rightarrow \pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r)\rightarrow\ldots.$$
nodes.statement_short: Long exact sequence.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Combining shows both that this long exact sequence breaks up into short exact sequences and that $$\widetilde{\nu^{n+1}_r}(R)\oplus\pi_n(K(R)/p^r)\overset{\sim}{\rightarrow}\pi_n(\mathrm{TC}(R)/p^r),$$ as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Split sequences.

nodes.name: Identification of $\widetilde{\nu^m_1}$ with $\widetilde{\nu^m}$
conclusions: $$\widetilde{\nu^m_1}(R)= \widetilde{\nu^m}(R):=\operatorname{coker}( 1 - C^{-1}: \Omega^m_R \to \Omega^m_R / d \Omega^{m-1}_R)$$

nodes.name: Reduced Frobenius $\overline{F}$ on de Rham--Witt groups
nodes.statement: As in \cite[Sec.~4]{Morrow-HW}, we have a natural map \[ \overline{F}: W_r \Omega_R^{m} \to W_r \Omega_R^{m}/ d V^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \] for an arbitrary $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$ which factors the Frobenius $F: W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \to W_r \Omega_R^{m}$.

nodes.name: Projection $\pi$ and the map $\pi - \overline{F}$
nodes.statement: Let $\pi: W_r \Omega_R^{m} \to W_r \Omega_R^{m}/ d V^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m}$ be the natural projection and consider the map \begin{equation} W _r \Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{\pi - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/ (d V^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m}) .\end{equation}

nodes.name: The map $\pi - \overline{F}$
nodes.statement: W _r \Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{\pi - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/ (d V^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m}) .
nodes.label: piminusF

nodes.name: Logarithmic de Rham--Witt forms as kernel of $\pi-\overline{F}$
nodes.statement: By \cite[Cor. 4.2(iii)]{Morrow-HW}, the map $\pi - \overline{F}$ has kernel given by the logarithmic forms, i.e., we have a short exact sequence \begin{equation} 0 \to W_r \Omega_{R, \mathrm{log}}^{m} \to W _r \Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{\pi - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/ (d V^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m}) .\end{equation}
conclusions: the map $\pi - \overline{F}$ has kernel given by the logarithmic forms

nodes.name: Logarithmic forms as kernel of $\pi-\overline{F}$
nodes.statement: 0 \to W_r \Omega_{R, \mathrm{log}}^{m} \to W _r \Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{\pi - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/ (d V^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m}) .
nodes.label: piminusF2

nodes.name: Identification of $\widetilde{\nu}_r^m$
nodes.statement: For any $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $R$, we have a natural identification of graded abelian groups \[ \widetilde{\nu_r^m}(R) \simeq \mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F}). \]
conclusions: we have a natural identification of graded abelian groups \[ \widetilde{\nu_r^m}(R) \simeq \mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F}). \]
nodes.label: identifytwiddle

nodes.name: Proof of Identification of $\widetilde{\nu}_r^m$
nodes.statement: We claim that the map $\pi - \overline{F}$ is surjective locally in the \'etale topology and the cokernel satisfies rigidity for henselian pairs. The first claim follows because the composite map \[ W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \stackrel{R}{\to} W_r \Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{\pi - \overline{F}} W_r \Omega_R^{m}/dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \] actually lifts to the map $W_{r+1}\Omega_R^{m} \xrightarrow{R - F} W_r \Omega_R^{m}$, which is a surjection in the \'etale topology thanks to \cite[Cor. 4.1(ii)]{Morrow-HW}. Second, let $(R, I)$ be a henselian pair of $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebras. To see that $\mathrm{coker}( \pi - \overline{F})$ is rigid, we can imitate the strategy of Proposition~\ref{toyFprigidityTC}. Namely, we let $L$ denote the kernel of the surjection $W_r \Omega_R^{m} / dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \to W_r \Omega_{R/I}^{m}/d V^{r-1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m}$ and contemplate the commutative diagram \[ \xymatrix{ & & W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \\ W_{r+1} \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \ar[rru]^{R - F} \ar[r]^R & W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \ar[d] \ar[r]^{\psi} & L \ar[d] \\ W_{r+1} \Omega_R^{m} \ar[d] \ar[r]^R & W_r \Omega_R^{m}\ar[d] \ar[r]^-{\pi - \overline{F}} & W_r \Omega_R^{m} / dV^{r-1} \Omega_R^{m} \ar[d] \\ W_{r+1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} \ar[r]^R & W_{r} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} \ar[r]^-{\pi - \overline{F}} & W_r \Omega_{R/I}^{m}/ d V^{r-1} \Omega_{R/I}^{m} }.\] To prove rigidity, it suffices by the snake lemma to show that $\psi:W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m} \to L$ is a surjection. Note that the kernel $L$ is surjected upon by the relative forms $W_r \Omega_{(R, I)}^{m}$; this follows easily from the fact that $\Omega_R^{m} \to \Omega_{R/I}^{m}$ is a surjection. Thus, the surjectivity of $\psi$ now follows from the surjectivity of $R - F: W_{r+1} \Omega^{m}_{(R, I)} \to W_r \Omega^{m}_{(R, I)}$ given by Lemma~\ref{lemma_drw1}. Now we prove the proposition.
